articles.standfirst: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Levante y al Sevilla en el Ciutat de València, correspondiente a la jornada 8 de LaLiga
articles.summary: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Levante y al Sevilla en el Ciutat de València, correspondiente a la jornada 8 de LaLiga
articles.body: El Levante recibe al Sevilla este lunes (21:00 h) en el Ciutat de València, en el cierre de una jornada que llega tras el parón de selecciones. Los granotas son decimoséptimos con 5 puntos en seis partidos (el de la jornada 6 ante el Athletic está aplazado al 21 de octubre) y no ganan desde el 5-2 al Betis. El Sevilla, en cambio, es quinto con 13 puntos, cuatro victorias, un empate y dos derrotas, y llega tras caer por 1-3 ante el Barcelona en el Sánchez-Pizjuán, con triplete de Raphinha. Favorito para el partido entre Levante y Sevilla El partido llega muy igualado en el mercado de las casas de apuestas. Betfair paga la victoria del Levante a 2.7, el empate a 3.25 y el triunfo del Sevilla a 2.6. Los números de la temporada inclinan la balanza hacia el visitante. El Sevilla no ha perdido fuera de casa (dos triunfos y un empate, con cinco goles a favor y dos en contra) y el Levante ha sumado solo un gol en sus cuatro salidas. El factor local, en cualquier caso, mantiene al conjunto valenciano en la pelea. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan es una opción atractiva dentro de las apuestas deportivas, por la fragilidad de los dos. El Levante ha encajado 12 goles en seis partidos y ha marcado en tres de ellos, con el 5-2 al Betis y el 2-4 ante el Barcelona como ejemplos de su juego abierto en casa: en los dos partidos en el Ciutat ha visto puerta y ha recibido goles. El Sevilla, por su parte, ha marcado en seis de sus siete partidos y ha recibido goles en cinco, con encuentros como el 2-1 al Rayo, el 1-3 al Atlético o el 1-3 frente al Barça. Con estos datos, el sí paga a 1.8, por 1.9 del caso contrario Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta a un partido con tantos. Los encuentros del Levante han acabado con más de 2.5 goles en cuatro de sus seis partidos (3-0 en Cornellà, 5-2, 2-4 y 3-1 en Villarreal), mientras que el Sevilla ha superado esa barrera en cuatro de siete. Algunos modelos estadísticos proyectan alrededor de cuatro goles. Los dos 0-0 del Levante ante Osasuna y Málaga, ambos lejos de casa, recuerdan que la tendencia es muy distinta en El Ciutat. El más de 2.5 goles paga en Betfair a 2, frente a 1.72 del menos de 2.5. Ganar ambas partes El mercado de ganar ambas partes, que un equipo se imponga en las dos mitades, es de riesgo alto pero con potencial de cuota. La apuesta es el Sevilla, por varios motivos: lleva dos victorias fuera, tiene un ataque en racha (10 goles en siete jornadas) y se enfrenta a un rival que ha recibido goles en los seis partidos que ha disputado menos en dos. Eso sí, el Levante ha demostrado que puede mantener el tipo en casa, como en el 5-2 al Betis y en la reacción ante el Barcelona, así que conviene tomar esta selección como una apuesta de valor y no como una certeza. Betfair paga la victoria del Sevilla en ambas partes a 9, misma que la del Levante.

articles.title: Swiss Darts Trophy 2026: Jonny Clayton defeats Luke Humphries to secure fourth Euro Tour title
articles.summary: Jonny Clayton picked up his first ranking title of 2026 and his fourth Euro Tour title by clinching the Swiss Darts Trophy with an 8-4 win over Luke Humphries; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
It marks Clayton's first European title of 2026, his first ranking title of the year and his fourth Euro Tour win overall.

The victory for Clayton also books the Welshman his spot at the Grand Slam of Darts in November.

There was not much separating Clayton and Humphries in the contest, with the former finding the better doubling but the world No 2 with the better scoring.

The crucial moment came in the 10th leg when, after nine holds of throw, Clayton finally got the advantage by taking out 26.

From there, Clayton held on tops and then broke Humphries once again with 46 on D16 to claim the Swiss Darts Trophy.

"It was a great game and a great game to be involved in. Luke on his doubles gave me the chance," Clayton said after his win.

"If you want to win these trophies you have to beat people like Luke. It is confidence and a spot in the Grand Slam.

"Winning my fourth, to win tournaments, you have to beat the best. You have to beat the boys on form and we were both on form.

"I am lucky to get through that. It is always good to have confidence in any game of darts.

"Who knows what happens - I feel good and I am enjoying my game."

Clayton made it into the final with a strong 7-4 win over world No 3 Gian van Veen, his 105 average proving the difference.

There was nothing separating the two in the early legs but then Clayton took control with a 161 finish on the bull for the first of his breaks of throw.

That gave him a two-leg lead which he kept hold of as Van Veen fumbled on the outer ring, eventually clinching the match on D4.

The Welshman started his evening with a 6-2 victory over Karel Sedlacek in the quarter-finals. The Welshman reeled off two sets of three legs in a row to claim the dominant win with three breaks of throw.

World No 2 Humphries booked his spot in another final with a 7-4 win over Mensur Suljovic, a staggering 111.17 average showing Humphries' class.

Humphries was 2-0 down but with three 13-dart legs and a 14-dart leg, rattled off four legs in a row to move ahead.

It then became a game of breaks as the Austrian and Englishman traded blows for five legs until Humphries eventually held his nerve in the 11th leg to send Suljovic out.

Humphries made it into the semis with a strong 6-3 victory over Cristo Reyes. It was a battle between the pair, but Humphries' scoring proved the difference as he took our for of the last five legs to seal the deal.

Earlier, Suljovic dropped just one leg for an imperious 6-1 victory over Dirk van Duijvenbode in the quarter-finals, the Austrian taking four legs in a row from 2-1 up. It marked Suljovic's first Euro Tour semi-final since 2021.

To start his night, Van Veen rallied from three legs down to secure a 6-5 last-leg decider against Bradley Brooks. Van Veen's scoring started off slow but he fought back well, using the pressure to his advantage to get the result over the line.

articles.title: KC Concepcion ruled out with head injury, Browns cut Jets lead to 7-3
articles.summary: The Browns have lost wide receiver KC Concepcion for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets.
articles.body:
The Browns have lost wide receiver KC Concepcion for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets.

Concepcion stayed down after taking a big hit to the head from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick while trying to catch a pass. Fitzpatrick was penalized for the hit and Concepcion was eventually able to head to the locker room under his own power.

The Browns quickly announced that Concepcion has been ruled out with a head injury.

The penalty — Fitzpatrick's second personal foul on the drive — moved the Browns to the Jets' 12-yard-line, but they couldn't get much closer and settled for an Andre Szmyt field goal to cut the Jets' lead to 7-3 with 3:27 to play in the first quarter.

articles.title: Brent Venables insists Oklahoma’s upset win over Texas went ‘according to script’
articles.summary: Oklahoma football may have surprised many people this week, upsetting Texas 27-24. While many people may have doubted that they would win coming into the ga...
articles.body:
Oklahoma football may have surprised many people this week , upsetting Texas 27-24. While many people may have doubted that they would win coming into the game, head coach Brent Venables knew it was their destiny to walk away with the victory.

"Made the plays when we needed to make them, wasn't always pretty… went according to script," Venables said via Evan Kamikow of News9.

It was a slow first half for Oklahoma, but it was the second half where things started to work in their favor. They outscored Texas 20-7 in the second half, and John Mateer felt like he was a part of the longest fourth quarter of his life .

As for Texas, they did the complete opposite, starting the game fast but not being able to get anything going in the second half. With the loss, it wouldn't be a surprise to see them drop in the top 25 AP polls.

articles.title: Rutgers Listed as 4.5 Point Underdogs Against Maryland
articles.summary: Underdog Scarlet Knights looking to extend winning streak against Terrapins
articles.body:
The betting lines for Week 7 of the college football season have opened, with Rutgers being listed as 4.5-point underdogs on the road against Maryland, according to FanDuel. Both teams currently sit winless in Power Four play, with Maryland suffering multi-score losses to Virginia Tech, UCLA, Nebraska and Ohio State, and Rutgers losing to Boston College, USC, and Indiana.

Both teams have coaches on the hot seat. Both teams are eyeing this game as their best opportunity to get at least one win in the Big Ten this season. ESPN's matchup predictor gives Maryland a 60.7% chance to win the game. The game will also be Maryland's Homecoming game, meaning that the atmosphere should be a little more hostile than usual for Rutgers.

This game will be a clash of offensive styles, as the Terrapins lean on a very pass-heavy attack while Rutgers uses the run-heavy format that it always has under head coach Greg Schiano. So far this season, Maryland quarterback Malike Washington has thrown for 1,352 yards on 223 attempts for seven touchdowns and six interceptions. Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan has thrown for 775 yards on 92 attempts for seven touchdowns and five interceptions. Lonergan has also missed significant time this season due to injury, which is why his overall passing attempts numbers are low.

On the ground, Rutgers running back Antwan Raymond has picked up 469 rushing yards on 89 carries while also scoring four touchdowns. Maryland running back Dejuan Williams has earned 242 rushing yards on 29 carries while adding three touchdowns. KJ Duff continues to shine in the Rutgers wide receiver room, as he already has 628 receiving yards for seven touchdowns, while Maryland's leading receiver Chris Durr Jr. has 476 yards on 46 catches for four touchdowns.

Neither team's defense has looked good in Power Four play this season, as the Terrapins have surrendered 35 points to Virginia Tech, 54 points to UCLA, 48 points to Nebraska and 45 points to Ohio State, while Rutgers defense has surrendered 28 points to Boston College, 42 points to USC and 47 points to Indiana. Due to the poor performances of both defenses, FanDuel has set the over/under at 54.5 points.

The Terrapins hold the all-time advantage in the series over the Knights, 12-9, with Rutgers winning the last two matchups in 2024 and 2025.

Kickoff time for Rutgers at Maryland is set for 12:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, October 17, inside SECU Stadium in College Park. Live coverage for the game will be available on BTN.

articles.title: Lotería Nacional, sorteo del Día de la Hispanidad 2026: premios, cuándo es y cuánto cuesta el décimo del 12 de octubre
articles.summary: Los detalles del sorteo
articles.body: El tradicional sorteo del 12 de octubre reparte 105 millones en premios, con un décimo ganador que puede alcanzar los 15 millones de euros. El próximo domingo 12 de octubre, coincidiendo con el Día de la Hispanidad y la festividad de la Virgen del Pilar, Loterías y Apuestas del Estado celebra uno de los sorteos más esperados del calendario: el Sorteo Extraordinario del Día de la Hispanidad 2025. La emisión consta de diez series de 100.000 billetes cada una, con un precio de 150 euros por billete (15 euros por décimo). En total, se pondrán en juego 105 millones de euros en premios, y el afortunado que acierte las cinco cifras, serie y fracción exactas del primer premio podrá ganar hasta 15 millones de euros. El sorteo se celebrará el lunes 12 de octubre a las 21:00 horas (hora peninsular). Podrá seguirse en directo a través de RTVE y los canales oficiales de Loterías y Apuestas del Estado, además de consultarse los resultados completos minutos después en su web. La duración estimada es de 30 minutos, con el anuncio de todos los premios principales y las terminaciones a partir de las 21:30 horas. En total, más de 3,5 millones de décimos recibirán algún tipo de premio. Conviene recordar que Hacienda retiene un 20% de los premios superiores a 40.000 euros, por lo que tanto el primer como el premio especial estarán sujetos a dicha retención. Participar en el sorteo cuesta 15 euros por décimo, una inversión que podría transformarse en millones. La fecha del 12 de octubre, además de ser la Fiesta Nacional de España, es un día de gran carga simbólica: conmemora la llegada de Cristóbal Colón a América en 1492 y la unión cultural e histórica entre los pueblos hispanoamericanos. Cada año, este sorteo extraordinario rinde homenaje a esa efeméride bajo el mismo espíritu de fortuna y celebración que impregna la jornada. Desde su creación, el Sorteo del Día de la Hispanidad se ha consolidado como uno de los grandes hitos del calendario de la Lotería Nacional, a la altura del Sorteo de Navidad o del Sorteo de El Niño.

Dominic Zvada comes back on for a 56-yard field goal and makes it. is now 2 for 4 on field goals, all of which have been at least 50 yards.

The Giants remain their own worst enemies.

The Giants get a couple first downs, then fall behind the chains.

The Giants get the ball to start the second half down 9. Can they do anything to turn the game around?

Zvada misses his second kick of the game, pushing the 57-yard attempt to the left. Washington takes a 12-3 lead into halftime. The Giants will get the ball to start the second half.

Two passes glance off of Malik Nabers' fingers, the second of which (probably) would have been a touchdown.

The Giants' defense does its job and limits Washington to another field goal. Washington leads 12-3 inside of the two-minute warning.

The Giants once again run face-first into the Commanders' defense out of a condensed set, followed by a Jameis Winston sack-fumble. Washington recovers at the 28-yard line.

The Giants bring pressure on 3rd down and force another 3-and-out. Jack Kelly very nearly blocks the ensuing punt.

Ar'Darius Washington replaces (an apparently injured) Tyler Nubin at safety.

The Giants have no answers for the Commanders' Vikings-style blitz attack and are forced to punt again.

Washington is able to move the ball again, but the Giants force a field goal attempt after the pressure once again gets to Jayden Daniels. The Commanders lead 9-3 with 8:57 left in the first half. Can the Giants figure out something on offense before halftime?

Trace Ford is seeing the field for the Giants.

Down goes Daniels as the Giants sack Jayden Daniels again, forcing another 3-and-out. Dru Phillips gets the sack on a blitz as Kayvon Thibodeaux works inside to create the lane for Phillips.

The Giants go 3-and-out as they commit to the run, but can't find any yardage. They need to find a way to get into rhythm.

Can the Giants get their offense going on their second possession?

The Giants force a 3-and-out as Tremaine Edmunds and Darius Alexander force Jayden Daniels to throw the ball away on 3rd and long.

Abdul Carter makes his presence known, running Jayden Daniels down for the sack.

The Giants struggle to find anything like traction on offense, and their opening drive fizzles after Dominic Zvada misses a 50-yard field goal attempt. His first miss as a professional.

Darnell Mooney is back in the game, but the Giants are moving backward.

The Giants' wide receiver depth is already being tested as Darnell Mooney is staying on the ground.

Jameis Winston picks up a long first down and now it's McCarthy time.

Washington knifes through the Giants' defense on their opening drive with big catches by Chig Okonkwo and runs by Bill Crosky-Merritt. Washington leads 6-0 after a missed extra point.

The Giants win the coin toss and will defer to the second half. The Commanders will get the ball to start the game.

Winds will be between 10 and 15 mph, with gusts up to 26 mph. Ball security, which has been a major focus for Giants head coach John Harbaugh, will be a major factor. articles.title: Jaguars clip Eagles’ wings with walk-off field goal in London thriller
articles.summary: From delirium to devastation – and back again – a lot can happen in a second.
articles.body: From delirium to devastation – and back again – a lot can happen in a second. As the clock ticked down toward the end of a pulsating game at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Jacksonville Jaguars fans began to flock towards the nearest exit. Philadelphia kicker Jake Elliott had just nailed a field goal with only eight seconds left to play to give the Eagles what would surely be a nail-biting win. But just as quickly as the Philly fans began planning their night on the town in London, Jaguars running back Ameer Abdullah threw a wrench in those plans. Weaving his way through the desperate tackle attempts, Abdullah returned the corresponding kick off to field goal range before being tackled with just one second on the clock. Cam Little then stepped up and silenced the Philadelphia faithful, sealing a 19-17 victory for the Jags. “One of the craziest games, maybe the craziest game I’ve ever been a part of,” Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence said after the dramatic win. “And I’ve been in some pretty wild ones.” ‘I cost us that game’ After going in at halftime with the Eagles leading 14-7, the action had completely dried up for much of the second half. A Jags field goal was the only score in the first 27 minutes following the break. Both quarterbacks struggled to find any rhythm; constant flags stifled any semblance of flow and the football had seemingly become secondary to those in attendance. But out of nowhere, the game exploded into life. Lawrence, the sixth-year signal caller, found receiver Parker Washington in the end zone with just over three minutes left in the game to give Jacksonville the lead. Little, however, missed the extra point leaving the Jaguars up just 16-14. A field goal would surely be all the Eagles needed to take the win and after a punt from each side, Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts marched Philly’s O down the field. It was a side of Philadelphia’s offense that had been lacking all second half. The team seemed to have finally found the precision and set up Elliott’s field goal perfectly. Despite the Philadelphia fans’ best efforts, however, this wasn’t to be enough and the Eagles will now return stateside on the back of a devastating loss. “At the end of the day I didn’t make the right decision, and it cost us the game,” Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said after the defeat. “There’s no other way around it. There’s nothing really else to say about that. It’s just I didn’t do my job good enough in that situation.” Siranni admitted he took full responsibility for the defeat in front of his team after the loss. “The guys fought so hard … and I cost us that game.” The 28-year-old Hurts was also quick to shoulder the blame for the lack of the Eagles’ effectiveness in offense. “Offensively, there was not enough out there for us to do. We didn’t perform well enough. I didn’t perform well enough.” A Philly atmosphere in London This game was advertised as a home game for the Jaguars, but the atmosphere was anything but Jacksonville-friendly. From the tube to the pubs, Eagles fans were all you could see. In the stadium it was no different. Waves of green dominated the 61,322 in attendance and if the jerseys weren’t a giveaway, the noise was. “Our fans showed up. It was great,” Hurts said after the game. “It was great to feel that energy and to see how they showed up when we didn’t do enough.” From start to finish, Lawrence and the Jags struggled with the deafening atmosphere from the majority-Philly crowd. “You could see that they had some issues handling some of that noise in that game,” Sirianni said of the impact the Philadelphia fans had on Jacksonville. And Lawrence clearly agreed. “I thought it was supposed to be a home game for us over here,” the Jaguars quarterback joked afterward. “Usually we have more fans, being the Jags and playing over here so much. This was really the only time I could remember where it was so lopsided.” But, ultimately, it’s the Jacksonville few that will have the last laugh as they prepare to stay in London for another week, where the team will face the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium. For Philadelphia, this now represents three consecutive losses amidst a difficult juncture that the team needs to get through. The ever-poised Hurts, however, stayed calm in defeat. “There’s so much opportunity to grow, so much for us to be better at and we just continue on our journey, gelling and obviously staying locked arms and staying together as a team,” Hurts added. Eagles will host the Carolina Panthers next week at Lincoln Financial Field.

articles.title: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning's words immediately came back to bite him in awful loss to UCLA
articles.summary: Dylan Raiola went 6-19 with two interceptions before being benched as the Oregon Ducks committed seven turnovers in a stunning home loss to UCLA.
articles.body: This was supposed to be the year. The Oregon Ducks started the 2026 college football season as a consensus top-five team under head coach Dan Lanning. They brought back Dante Moore and added Dylan Raiola, a former starter at Nebraska, as a backup quarterback. They had a highly-paid roster full of former top recruits, along with impactful transfer portal additions. They were coming off back-to-back College Football Playoff appearances with a combined 26-3 record across the regular and postseason in 2024-2025. Some suggested it was the best team Oregon's ever had. Almost immediately, however, the Ducks started taking on water. Boise State nearly pulled off the upset in Eugene in week one. Then Oklahoma State finished their upset bid in week two behind a dominant offensive performance. DAN LANNING BLASTS USC AFTER OREGON'S WIN, AS LINCOLN RILEY OFFICIALLY ENTERS HOT SEAT IN LA After an 84-0 shellacking of Portland State, the Ducks went into Los Angeles for a pivotal game against USC at the Coliseum and finally seemed to turn the corner. When Moore left the game after an awful hit from a USC linebacker, Raiola stepped up and looked even better. Moore went 19-25 for 289 yards and two touchdowns, helping secure a 41-27 win to seemingly save Oregon's season. Lanning took the opportunity after the win to make a statement about the Ducks' program and where their focus lies. "I guess if you're interested in winning football games and you're from this area, you should go to Oregon," Lanning said, referring to high school players from the Los Angeles and Southern California area. "If you want to go to a Chris Brown concert, you should go here." Fast-forward two weeks and Lanning's words immediately came back to bite him. The Ducks on Saturday hosted UCLA under first-year head coach Bob Chesney. The Bruins, after years of mediocrity, have looked dramatically improved thus far in 2026, though against overmatched opponents like Cal, Purdue, and Maryland. Saturday marked their first test, a road game in one of the toughest environments in college football, against a team with aspirations of reaching and winning the College Football Playoff. For Lanning, it was an opportunity to back up his statement, that if you want to play winning football, you come to Oregon. They lost. The Ducks played one of the sloppiest games from any program in recent memory, somehow managing to turn the ball over an incredible seven times. They had five lost fumbles, and recovered the ball on a sixth fumble. Raiola was so awful, going 6-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions, that Lanning benched him for third stringer Brock Thomas. Four plays for 22 yards and a punt, a one-yard touchdown drive after a Nico Iamaleava fumble, three plays for zero yards, and four plays for 20. 12 plays for 43 yards, and it got worse from there. Much worse. Here's the drive chart for Oregon's second quarter: 16 plays for 25 yards, two punts, two fumbles, and an interception. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. The Ducks did pick up more yards in the third quarter though, going three plays for two yards, four plays for 22 yards and a fumble, and two plays for seven yards and another pick. That's 31 total yards and only two turnovers instead of three. Progress! While Oregon did have a better run in the fourth quarter, working around another fumble to kick a field goal and finally score their second touchdown of the game with 2:16 remaining, the two-point conversion attempt to tie the score at 17-17 failed. Fittingly, the game ended on Oregon fumbling while trying to run a series of laterals down the field as time expired. As Lanning said, "If you care about winning games, and you're from LA, come to Oregon." Or apparently UCLA. Obviously, Moore being out hurt the Ducks' offense, but seven turnovers? Only 272 yards, at home, against a UCLA team that unquestionably has inferior talent? At one point, Oregon went six straight drives without picking up a first down. At one point, excluding the end of the second quarter, the Ducks turned the ball over on six out of nine drives. That is ... remarkable. From 2023-2025, Lanning built Oregon into one of the most consistent teams in the country. They were 38-5, and went undefeated in their first season in the Big Ten to secure the number one overall seed in the 2024-2025 playoff. For most of that run, his teams were seen as well coached and disciplined. articles.body:
Welcome to Bleacher Report's coverage of TNA Bound for Glory 2026.

Here is a look at the card from Sunday's show:

Fabian Aichner vs. KC Navarro vs. Cedric Alexander vs. Ryan Nemeth vs. BDE vs. Rich Swann (Scramble, X-Division Championship)

Nic Nemeth vs. Leon Slater (TNA World Title)

Let's take a look at everything that happened at this year's Bound for Glory PPV.

The first match of the night saw Sosa take on what the announcers called his biggest opponent to date, Edwards.

At just 21 years old, Sosa is in a similar spot to where Slater was when he first joined TNA. If he can keep impressing officials, he will have a long career ahead of him.

The pace was quick whenever Sosa was in control, and whenever Edwards took over, it became a little more hard-hitting.

This was a decent match, but it felt more like it belonged on TV than on a PPV. This did not have the feel of taking place at the biggest show of the year for TNA.

Things picked up in the second half and made it a little more exciting, especially whenever Sosa took to the skies.

Sosa ended up taking out Alisha Edwards when she got involved, but that distraction allowed Eddie to gain the upper hand momentarily, but Sosa finished him off with a Headshot for the win.

Sosa got great elevation on his dropkick.

TNA's smaller ring takes some getting used to if you are not familiar with it. You barely notice, but it just feels off somehow.

Alisha Edwards does a good job being active in the match without distracting too much.

Aichner was out first for this Scramble match that went from six to seven competitors when Amazing Red revealed he would be involved during the TNA Hall of Fame ceremony.

The other competitors included BDE, Alexander, Navarro, Swann, Red and the younger Nemeth brother, Ryan. Most of these guys qualify as high-flyers, so we knew we were in for a show, but the inclusion of Nemeth and Aichner gave those guys a base.

As expected, this match was fast-paced right out of the gate. There wasn't a single moment when nothing was happening in or outside the ring. Not every spot was memorable, but they all added to the overall entertainment.

Swann was one of the standouts, which is not surprising given his skills, but even with seven people all vying for the crowd's attention, it never felt like it was too chaotic to follow what was happening.

After several close calls, Red ended up pinning Navarro to become the new X-Division champion. The newly inducted Hall of Famer looked elated when he was handed the belt.

Amazing Red still wrestling at this level in 2026 is awesome.

Seeing Swann and Alexander together is always fun. It kind of makes us miss 205 Live.

Nemeth trying to shake everyone's hand only to eat a superkick was a funny way to start the match.

Red and Navarro had a nice sequence in the middle of the match.

Even though it took way too long to set up, the six-man Tower of Doom spot was kind of cool.

Allie and Kiera Hogan vs. Shayna Baszler and Zoey Serrano

Shayna Baszler made her TNA in-ring debut at Bound for Glory when she teamed with Serrano to take on Allie and Hogan for the Knockouts tag titles.

Hogan and Allie may have come into this as the champions, but they were also the underdogs in many ways. Baszler is known as a dangerous striker and submission artist, and Serrano is a powerhouse, so they bullied their opponents every chance they got.

This match had a steady pace, but it did feel like it moved a bit too slowly at times, especially when it took longer to set up a move than it should.

Baszler locked Allie in a choke and made her pass out to make her and Zoey the new Knockouts tag champs.

This match could have used a few more minutes and a couple of high spots, but having new champions is always nice. Baszler and Serrano work well together.

Result: Baszler and Serrano won the titles

It's nice to see Baszler back in the ring. She was never properly used in WWE.

In some ways, this was a WWE vs. AEW tag match when you look at where each woman came from before this.

Allie's little tribute to The Butcher was nice.

The Call Your Shot Gauntlet was up next. This match combines rules from a Battle Royal and standard Gauntlet match, so eliminations over the top rope happen until the final two competitors are left, and then they have a standard singles match to end it.

Here is the order of entry for the competitors:

The biggest portion of this match resembled a Battle Royal, and it included all of the usual tropes of that kind of bout. The fact that it was intergender also led to some interesting moments.

There were plenty of entertaining moments, but most of the entrants never felt like they had a chance to win, so most of the time was spent waiting for the most obvious eliminations. Sadly, some of the moments meant to be comedic fell flat.

The final four were Kaz, Francis, Styles and Miguel. When it was just Kazarian and Miguel left, the singles match began. They put on a good show, but it wasn't quite enough to elevate the whole long match.

Kazarian ended up getting the win while they were trading pinning combinations.

If Styles wants to make his own name, he should stop copying his dad's entrance right away.

Styles jumped way too early for a dropkick.

Dutch's one-armed slam on Styles looked good.

Cleary hitting a poison rana on Bronson was a cool spot.

Rehwoldt talking such a huge game as he was getting ready only to get tossed right out by Heather was kind of funny.

Ben Bishop took out Jada Stone on his way to the ring.

Mustafa Ali vs. Jason Hotch vs. John Skyler vs. Special Agent 0

The TNA International Championship was on the line in a Fatal 4-Way when Ali put the belt on the line against Hotch, Agent 0 and Skyler.

Hotch and Ali's last match at Lockdown was a banger, so there was a lot of pressure on them to do the same, which added even more pressure to Skyler and Agent 0.

For some reason, there was no commentary even though they were still at ringside, and when you add that to how poorly the audio was to the crowd, it made this feel way too quiet despite the fact that all four guys were going hard right away.

Weirdly, backing out of the stream and going back in seemed to fix the issue, so it was hard to say where the glitch occurred. There were also some graphical issues and lag at times.

Despite those technical issues, this was a very entertaining contest. Everyone involved was doing their best to make this an exciting bout, and they definitely succeeded. Hotch and Ali were definitely the standouts, but everyone contributed.

Hotch was able to steal the win by using a crucifix pin after Ali hit a 450, making him the new international champion.

Result: Hotch won the International Championship

Ali does a surprisingly good job playing a creepy heel who wants to intimidate women and children.

It's really a shame Ali never meshed well in WWE. He deserves to be on a bigger stage. Everything from his entrance to his ring work feels a cut above everyone else in TNA right now.

The way Ali hit the corner when he slid out of the ring looked nasty.

Ali hit a very nice 450 to put Tasha Steelz and Agent 0 through a table.

The Knockouts Championship was up for grabs when Brookside put it on the line against her rival, Hartwell. Mickie James served as the special guest referee.

There was a lot of trash talking before they locked up and started fighting for control. Hartwell is still beloved by fans, so it was easy for Brookside to get heat from the crowd with very simple heel tactics.

This felt like a personal fight between enemies, so it had good energy in that way, but it never felt like their physical intensity matched what was on their faces and what they were saying.

The match was decent, but it felt like it fell short of its potential. Both of these women are good in the ring, so it was surprising to see them take so long to find their groove. Once they did, things picked up a bit.

Xia tried to take the belt and leave at one point, but Indi made sure she didn'tmake it very far. She also got into an argument with James and slapped her, which led to James slapping her back and almost handing Hartwell the win.

Both women had some close falls, but it was Hartwell who emerged victorious as the new Knockouts champion.

It's great to see James still doing things in wrestling. She has been a constant in this business for a couple of decades.

The spot when Hartwell stopped Brookside's trash talk by shoving her into the apron was funny because of the close-up angle.

TNA has a new star on its roster, and he had his PPV debut this week when Caster took on TNA mainstay, Moose. As usual, Caster wrote a rap to insult his opponent on the way to the ring.

Moose tried to offer a handshake, but Max brushed him off. When Moose made a clean break in the corner, Caster pushed him. Moose fired back and knocked him down with one shoulder block.

The crowd was a little hard to hear at times throughout the night, but this was one of the times when the lack of noise was due to a lack of energy. It felt like the crowd just didn't care, which could partially be blamed on the placement of this match on the card.

Had this bout come earlier in the night, it might have been more exciting because it didn't have to follow a handful of title changes. There were no stakes, so there wasn't much of a reason to get invested unless you are a huge fan of one of these guys.

Other than a few spots that looked pretty good, there was nothing about this match that made most of it memorable. Had this been on a weekly TV show, it would have been good, but it did not feel like it belonged on a PPV, which is sad because Caster is actually a talented guy who is capable of more than this. We've seen it.

The final few minutes were definitely the best part. It felt like they had gotten used to each other, so we saw a few high-risk spots that worked out. The crowd woke up a bit, too. Moose was able to pick up the win with a Spear, spoiling Caster's debut.

Caster's rap could be seen as taking a shot at WWE, too.

Caster's dropkick off the chair caught Moose directly in the head. It did not look like a fun spot for him to take.

Caster hit a nice back body drop to send Moose into the steps. They lined it up about as well as you possibly could in that situation.

Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw, the former Joe Gacy and Dexter Lumis, had one of their biggest matches to date when they faced Matt and Jeff Hardy in a Falls Count Anywhere match. Syx destroyed a table with sledgehammers as they made their entrance.

The match got started when all four men started brawling before the Hardys had even gotten to the ring.

By design, this match was mayhem, and that was probably for the best. If they tried to work a standard tag match, it wouldn't have been nearly as enjoyable as this was. They fought all over the arena and concourse area.

Jeff ended up hitting a massive Swanton bomb through two tables from the second level of the crowd, but it looked like they had something even riskier planned when they set up some tables and ladders on the stage.

Unfortunately for them, Erick Redbeard showed up and slammed them through the tables instead. Syx was able to get the win, thanks in large part to Redbeard's interference. This was a fun mess of a match.

Kazarian revealed during a backstage promo that he plans to use his title shot for him and Styles to challenge for the TNA tag titles.

Has X-Pac commented about Syx yet? He should be their manager.

That table spot from Jeff was great. It's wild how he has done stuff like that for so long and can still walk.

articles.title: Jonny Clayton beats Luke Humphries to claim Swiss title
articles.summary: Jonny Clayton claims his first ranking title of the year by beating Luke Humphries in the Swiss Darts Trophy final.
articles.body:
Jonny Clayton claimed his first ranking title of the year by beating Luke Humphries in the Swiss Darts Trophy final.

Welshman Clayton began the day by beating Rob Cross 6-4 in the last-16 stage, returning to beat Karel Sedlacek 6-2 at the start of the evening session before a 7-4 semi-final victory against world number three Gian van Veen took him to the final.

World number two Humphries, who progressed in Basel with wins against Krzysztof Ratajski (6-0), Cristo Reyes (6-3) and Mensur Suljovic (7-4), was hoping to add to his recent success at the World Grand Prix.

However, world number five Clayton had other ideas and claimed an 8-4 victory in the Euro Tour event to also secure a place in November's Grand Slam of Darts.

The players had almost identical averages – 101.75 for Humphries and 101.68 for Clayton – but it was the latter's finishing that proved decisive as he claimed victory with a run of four successive legs from 4-4.

Clayton, who hit six 180s compared to four from his rival, had a checkout success of 61.54% compared to just 22.22% from Humphries.

articles.title: PDC Women's Series: Beau Greaves ends season with highest event-winning average in tournament history
articles.summary: Beau Greaves records the highest event-winning average in Women's Series history; Vicky Pruim secures World Darts Championship qualification; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports from November 14-22
articles.body:
Greaves - who had already claimed back-to-back titles in Event 21 and 22 on Saturday - averaged 98.75 on the way to her third successive competition title at Event 23, marking the highest event-winning average in the history of the Women's Series.

The Yorkshire native - who has won 17 out of a possible 24 Women's Series events this year - won all of her first four matches by a 4-0 scoreline, posting a stunning 103.66 average in her victory against Steph Clark.

She lost her first legs of the day in her 5-2 victory against Gemma Hayter in the quarter-finals, before beating Fallon Sherrock - who confirmed her own return to the World Darts Championship on Saturday - in the semi-final.

Her 5-3 victory against Jade Gofford in the final confirmed her first title of the day, before beating Laura van den Berg, Sara Walton, Vicky Martin and Lauren Bloomfield to reach the quarter-finals of event 24.

Wins against Kirsty Hutchinson and 20-year-old Italian Aurora Fochesato confirmed her second title of the day and her fourth of the weekend to cap off a successful 2026 season.

"I felt good," Greaves said. "I was chuffed with the first competition. I had some good averages and then I played steady enough in the second event.

"I knew I hadn't been playing at my best recently, but I've had some good moments today and I'm ready to build on it and take this into the back end of the year."

The Wigan double-header also saw Vicky Pruim claim the final spot on offer to compete in the World Darts Championship through the Women's Series rankings, joining Greaves, Sherrock, Hayter and Lisa Ashton.

"We gotta relay that as a offense, it starts from everybody top down. Ultimately, it’s on me." Commanders part-owner Magic Johnson offered his opinion on the game: "I’m in total disbelief my Commanders had such poor clock management in today’s overtime game against the Giants. All we had to do was kick the field goal and we would have won the game!" No NFC East team won this week. The Cowboys lost Thursday, and the Eagles fell earlier Sunday, but the Giants and Commanders couldn’t capitalize on the opening. articles.title: Petey Pablo Brings ‘Raise Up’ Anthem To Hornets Home Opener
articles.summary: Petey Pablo will headline the Hornets' Oct. 23 home opener. Fans get free shirts and exclusive merch. Here is the full plan.
articles.body:
Most home openers feature a generic national act that no one knows by name. The Charlotte Hornets are breaking that mold by booking a local legend who wrote the soundtrack for the entire region. Petey Pablo, the Grammy-nominated rapper, is set to headline the Hornets' 2026–27 home opener at Spectrum Center on Oct. 23. Representing the state in hip-hop for more than two decades, this Greenville, N.C. native considers the event a homecoming rather than merely a performance.

WSOC TV reports that the Friday night matchup against the Atlanta Hawks is scheduled to tip off at 7 p.m. The team has made it clear that this night is about celebrating local culture alongside the start of the season. Upon entering the arena, fans attending the home opener will get an exclusive "Raise Up" t-shirt. For years, that single track plus songs like "Carolina Colors" and "Vibrate" have been regular features at sporting events throughout the Carolinas. It is the kind of music that gets a crowd moving before the first bounce of the ball.

A limited-edition merchandise collaboration between Pablo and the Hornets will be sold at the Charlotte Hornets Fan Shop inside Spectrum Center on game night while supplies last. This move shows the team is ready to capitalize on the excitement surrounding a hometown hero. Those wishing to join the crowd can still purchase limited tickets for Opening Night via the team's website. The energy in the building should be electric when the beat drops and the crowd starts singing along to a song they know by heart.

This partnership highlights a shift in how the franchise views its connection to the local fan base. Instead of chasing big national names that might feel distant, they are doubling down on regional pride. The "Raise Up" anthem has been played in arenas across the state, but seeing it performed live by the man who wrote it adds a layer of authenticity that a playlist cannot match. It creates a moment where the players and the fans are united by a shared sound and a shared history.

For fans who cannot make it to the arena, the broadcast details are just as important as the halftime show. Throughout the season, all non-nationally televised games will air in the Charlotte area on Channel 9 or TV64. This ensures that the local audience can follow the team from the first tip-off to the final buzzer, no matter where they are. With the full schedule locked in, the Hornets face the Hawks at Spectrum Center on Oct. 23 at 7 p.m.

The team is building momentum with these local touches while they prepare for the grind of the regular season. The preseason is winding down, with the final preseason game against the Milwaukee Bucks taking place on Sunday, Oct. 11. After that, the focus shifts entirely to the main event. The home opener sets the tone for the year, and bringing in Petey Pablo sends a clear message to the league and the fans alike.

Per WSOC TV, the game will be broadcast locally if it is not picked up by a national network. The Hornets are ready to start their campaign with a celebration that feels personal and authentic. The combination of a local icon, exclusive gear, and a packed house makes this a night that fans will remember long after the final score. The stage is set for a memorable start to the 2026–27 season.

articles.title: Inside the bungled end-of-game sequence that led to shocking Commanders tie with Giants
articles.summary: Daniel Quinn and Jayden Daniels provided insight into what went horribly wrong on final play of Commanders-Giants tie
articles.body:
The Commanders worked their way into comfortable field-goal range with Jayden Daniels' pass to Treylon Burks, who went out of bounds at the New York Giants' 26-yard line with 1 minute, 2 seconds remaining.

Washington kept pushing for yards despite it being just a 43-yard field goal attempt. They ran Rachaad White to the right despite having no timeouts. He gained two yards on a play that ended with 55 seconds left.

The Commanders had plenty of time to discuss everything and ultimately decided to try one more play to make it a shorter field goal.

As we all know by now, this what happened next:

That led to a 27-27 tie against the New York Giants on Sunday at Northwest Stadium that left everyone stunned at what they just saw. It was a brutal sequence and awful display of situational awareness that cost Washington a win.

After the game, head coach Dan Quinn and quarterback Jayden Daniels explained what went down in a moment where everything fell apart.

"Leaving tonight with a tie feels like a loss," Quinn told on-site reporters in his postgame press conference . "The last sequence – you throw it out of bounds, you clock it, you give yourself a chance to kick it. We pride ourselves on those moments at the end of the game. After the first down run, we're still trying to gain more for the kick."

According to Quinn, the play called for Daniels to connect with a receiver on the left side – it looked to be tight end Ben Sinnott – or immediately throw it away if he wasn't open.

That didn't happen. The ball was snapped with 12 seconds left and, instead of throwing it to Sinnott or out of bounds, Daniels moved around the backfield, never threw it away and was tackled as seconds ticked away. The Commanders frantically tried to clock it at that point – most of their receivers were down the field — but never got set before time expired.

Daniels was asked after the game what he was supposed to do in that spot. His answer didn't directly address that.

"We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know it's an o-zone situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts from everybody, (from) the top down, but ultimately, it's on me."

Hindsight being what it is, Quinn said that play ever should've been run.

"The right call, honestly, is to clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot," Quinn said. "That's my responsibility, nobody else's. I'm gutted for our team."

That would've been the correct sequence. And, with as much time as was on the clock after White's run, Quinn could've heard and killed that final play call and simply let kicker Drew Stevens try to end it with a field-goal from a makable distance even with wet conditions.

"We were trying to gain more (yards)," Quinn said. "We don't need to. It's easy enough to say, 'let's clock it right here.'"

The Commanders didn't, and then the quarterback didn't throw it away. It was a situation overcomplicated unnecessarily that very likely gave a win away.

"The sequencing of that does not fall on (Daniels)," Quinn said. "It's an outside throw or a clock those are the two (options). Out-of-bounds throw or a clock, that has to come from me. I don't have to put him in that spot. I can do that earlier. We can finish with a kick. We don't need to gain more yards."

Quinn calls performance under pressure "winning time moments," and the Commanders thrived in those situations during a 2024 campaign that ended with a trip to the NFC title game .

The Commanders generally haven't been good in those situations since, and were awful there at the end of Sunday's game.

"Finding a way to nail that moment and that play – we have to do that 100 out of 100 times," Quinn said. "That falls onto me."

articles.title: Jayden Daniels weakly deflected full blame for his unacceptable OT mistake
articles.summary: This is not the expected leader answer you want to hear from Jayden Daniels after costing the Commanders a win.
articles.body:
It'll probably take a long time for Jayden Daniels to live down his brutal, game-ending mistake on Sunday. With the Washington Commanders staring at an easy field goal for the win in overtime against the New York Giants , Daniels inexplicably ate a sack on a pass play with a chance to throw it away. That decision, in turn, allowed the clock to run out and cemented a 27-27 tie between NFC East rivals because the Commanders did not have any timeouts.

In the aftermath of making such a mistake, you would hope to hear Daniels taking full responsibility. No qualifiers. No questions asked. That is what a quarterback of the team is supposed to do in front of the microphone, especially when the ultimate outcome of the play was all up to him anyway.

When asked to explain why he didn't throw the ball away during his postgame press conference, Daniels first pointed fingers at the rest of the Washington offense for not relaying to him that they didn't have timeouts to stop the clock in that situation. Then and only then did he say that ultimately the buck stops with him. Hmm. I don't know about that one. That doesn't sound like a quarterback who thinks it was all on him in a sequence where he could've simply looked up at the scoreboard before snapping the ball.

It doesn't, in fact, start with everyone. It starts with Daniels.

That's the quickest finger-pointing sandwiched in between a claim of responsibility, and it's a brutal look for the Commanders quarterback.

The Commanders are now 1-3-1 on the season after Daniels gave away what looked like a surefire divisional victory. Their next game is a Monday night road matchup with the juggernaut San Francisco 49ers. We'll see how the aftermath of this fiasco affects Daniels and company in such a tough spot as they try to keep their season afloat. Right now, it doesn't look good.

articles.title: How Deshaun Watson, Todd Monken summed up Browns' dismal day vs. Jets
articles.summary: The Browns offense struggled with mistakes and missed opportunity throughout their loss against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. ― The ending was a fitting one to the way the first 59-plus minutes essentially gone for the Browns on offense in their 17-12 loss to the New York Jets .

Quarterback Deshaun Watson was forced to try and keep a play alive, trying to avoid the pressure while hoping someone would break open downfield. Ultimately, it ended with Jets edge rusher Will McDonald IV sacking him, then stripping him of the football before recovering it at the Cleveland 17.

So, what you had on one play was the Jets' eighth sack of Watson, the fourth Browns fumble forced ― the third by Watson ― and the second fumble lost by them. If ever there was a play that pretty much summed up the mostly miserable offensive day for Cleveland, there it was.

"There was still hope," Watson said afterwards. "There were still opportunities. And again, they capitalized on it better than us. Then we had a penalty, a sack and some missed opportunities, but that happens. And again, get on the bus, get on this flight, watch the tape, see what we could have did better and learn and get ready for Baltimore next week because the opportunity might happen again."

Those opportunities had mostly produced good results for the Browns. Their three-game win streak entering the game was built on fourth-quarter comebacks or last-minute drives helping them pull a win out of the fire.

That wasn't the case against the Jets, who snapped their own three-game losing streak while snapping the Browns' three-game win streak. Even when the offense did provide that glimmer of hope as it did with Watson's 29-yard touchdown pass to Denzel Boston with 6:15 remaining to give them a 12-10 lead ― Andre Szmyt's point-after kick doinked off the upright ― it sort came out of nowhere after a run of stalled drives built off the Browns' own mistakes.

The Browns had punted on five consecutive drives before putting together a nine-play, 86-yard drice for their only touchdown of the game, They would follow that up with three possessions netting a combined minus-29 yards on 16 plays, with both fumbles ― the first being the back-breaking mishandled punt snap by Corey Bojorquez that set up the go-ahead Braelon Allen 22-yard touchdown with 3:01 remaining ― sandwiched around a punt right before the two minute warning.

"That's the part of growing as a team and coaches together collectively," Browns coach Todd Monken said. "And there's going to be some ups and downs as players and coaches and we're going to go back to work. We're going to watch the tape on the plane headed home and we're going to pick our big-boy pants up and try to figure out a way to get better. That's what you do and that's what we're paid to do. And it just wasn't good enough. I mean, you guys watched it."

Watson couldn't recapture the fourth-quarter magic that he possessed himself in a game where he was 15-of-33 of 155 yards with the Boston touchdown, the three fumbles, the one lost fumble and the eight sacks. However, it would be hard to completely pin it all on him.

The Browns lost wide receiver KC Concepcion with 4:53 left in the first quarter to a head injury sustained by a high, borderline-at-best hit by Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, the same player who ended former Browns running back Nick Chubb's 2023 season with a low blow in Pittsburgh. That required a shuffling of duties, including significantly more snaps for Isaiah Bond, who essentially took over Concepcion's role for the rest of the game.

Bond had three catches for 74 yards. He also was targeted seven times, but that included multiple drops, including a huge one with 2:25 remaining which would've put the Browns in Jets territory with a chance to win.

"Just a lack of concentration," Bond said. "I got to focus on the catch more."

Bond did have one of the Browns' bigger plays of the day, a 30-yarder to the Jets 45 early in the fourth quarter when they were trailing 10-6. However, what happened next summarized the two-steps-forward, three-steps-back day it was for that offense.

First-and-10 at the Jets 45 eventually became fourth-and-38 from the Browns 27. How, you might ask?

There was a pre-snap penalty on first down, followed by a 10-yard loss on a sack first-and-15, which was followed by a delay of game on second-and-25. There was a second-and-30 pass to Jerry Jeudy that was short and nearly intercepted by a diving Fitzpatrick, followed by an eight-yard loss by Watson on third down to make it fourth-and-38.

"Again, nothing was clean from special teams to offense," Monken said. "The only thing that we can actually say, our guys battled their rear ends off was on defense after the first drive and came up with some big stops when we needed. I mean, that's really what it came down to. And even then, all that being said, we haven't played a clean game yet. We just found a way in the other three games to get it done in the fourth quarter.

"I mean, let's be real about it. And we had the opportunity. We just did. We got the turnover, had the ball right there at the 40 and we didn't capitalize at that moment and that's what happens."

articles.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Deebo Samuel Injury Opens Door For 49ers Sleeper
articles.summary: Deebo Samuel's injury will lead to bigger days for several 49ers receivers, including Mike Evans.
articles.body:
The 49ers were already without Kyle Juszczyk on the offense, and now Deebo Samuel has gone down with a hamstring injury and has been ruled out for the rest of the game against the Seahawks.

Brock Purdy and Samuel have linked up well this season, with fantasy managers of both players enjoying the resurgence of the two.

Now with Samuel out, other receivers will need to step up for the 49ers' offense, especially Mike Evans and George Kittle.

Samuel has been a top fantasy player this year, with double-digit point tallies in Weeks 1, 3, and 4. The eighth-year man was ruled out with a hamstring injury after going down hard on the field.

Samuel's status will need to be monitored heading into Week 6 against the Commanders. If Samuel is good to go, he should a starter for fantasy managers.

Evans has been dealing with injuries of his own, but he has been another top target for Purdy downfield.

With Samuel dealing with his hamstring injury, managers should expect Evans to be Purdy's top receiver.

Evans has also recorded three double-digit point weeks this season, and he continues to perform at a high level for the 49ers, despite his injury struggles.

Evans is a must-start wide receiver, with or without Samuel in the offense.

Kittle has been a consistent fantasy pick when healthy, and he continues to show out for the 49ers, picking up an average of 16.1 fantasy points this season.

Kittle's best outing this season came against the Cardinals, which saw him tally 26.2 fantasy points on six receptions for 82 yards and two touchdowns.

Samuel's injury will lead to an increase in Kittle's targets, cementing him as a must-start tight end.

Brock Purdy continues to be one of the best quarterbacks in the league, with an overall QB3 ranking. Purdy is averaging 25.1 fantasy points this season, and even without Samuel, he ranks as a must-start quarterback.

Purdy will use Evans and Kittle as his top two receivers, and he won't forget that he has Christian McCaffrey to look to on the ground.

Fantasy managers of Samuel will be concerned for his Week 6 status, but fantasy managers of other 49er players should have no fear for Week 6.

Mike Evans and George Kittle look to be the biggest beneficiaries from Samuel's injury, and Purdy's consistency keeps him as a QB1.

articles.title: Broncos rally late for 23-17 win, send Chargers to 0-5
articles.summary: The Denver offense didn't show much improvement, but the Broncos got a win.
articles.body:
The Broncos still have plenty of work to do on the offensive side of the ball, but they'll get a chance to do it coming off of a win.

Head coach Sean Payton's decision to take back offensive playcalling responsibilities didn't lead to a clear improvement over previous weeks, but the unit was able to do enough to take advantage of Chargers mistakes in the fourth quarter to pull out a win. The 23-17 win moves them to 3-2 on the season and it leaves the Chargers to wait at least another week for their first win.

The Chargers scored a pair of touchdowns in the third quarter to jump into a 17-10 lead and they had a chance to pin the Broncos deep in their own territory with a punt with around 10 minutes left to play. Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh opted to go for it on fourth-and-1 from his own 41-yard-line, however, and Justin Herbert was stuffed way short on a sneak.

Bo Nix threw a touchdown pass to Courtland Sutton on the ensuing drive and Broncos defensive lineman D.J. Jones forced a Herbert fumble on the ensuing drive. The Broncos opted to kick a field goal after their drive stalled on the 1-yard-line and then added another after safety Brandon Jones picked Herbert off on the next Chargers possession.

Herbert now has nine turnovers on the season and the Chargers helped set up the first Broncos touchdown of the day with another turnover, so it was another chapter in the nightmare that has been unfolding for the team since Week 1. They'll be in Kansas City next Sunday to face a well-rested Chiefs team that's looking to move to 5-0.

The Broncos only had 95 yards of offense in the second half, they went 1-of-12 on third downs and they had no first downs on any of the drives that were not set up by Chargers turnovers, so Payton certainly didn't correct all that was wrong when Davis Webb was sending in the plays. He'll have a short week to try to make progress and a tough defense to work against in Seattle on Thursday night.

articles.title: Joe Burrow tosses four TDs in Week 5
articles.summary: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in Week 5
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow completed 23 of 32 passes for 190 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in the Week 5 game against the Miami Dolphins , while running four times for 10 yards.

Why it matters: Burrow's yardage total was a season low, but his four TD passes were a season high. He has completed 71.4 percent of his pass attempts in four of his five games, too. He remains a top-tier QB1 in all fantasy leagues.

articles.title: This is a good time for Miami Dolphins to take a break | D'Angelo
articles.summary: The Dolphins slipped to 0-5 after a 31-24 loss to Joe Burrow and the Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium. The game sends Miami into a bye week.
articles.body:
MIAMI GARDENS — Chop Robinson was so desperate to celebrate in a season where such moments have been rare, he got off the ground and started mimicking chopping wood as Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow lay there late in the fourth quarter wondering how the Miami Dolphins edge rusher arrived so quickly.

And much like the season has gone, that feel-good moment ended in an instant, the tell being the yellow flag on the ground. Robinson then learned because of his excitement to get to the quarterback the infraction was on him for being offside.

But it was to his, and the Dolphins, credit the play was still important. Because the way this game started, and the way quarterback Malik Willis was giving away the football as if the Dolphins were having a fire sale, Miami could have folded so much sooner.

"That's a step forward," receiver Kevin Coleman said. "First half didn't go as planned, but second half … you got to be a four-quarter team."

The Dolphins slipped to 0-5 after a 31-24 loss to Burrow and the Bengals at Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday. The game sends Miami into a bye week that many teams would not welcome coming so early, but probably is good for one this young and one that is facing adversity every week.

And if ever there was a sign this is the time, it occurred on the sideline in the second half when running back Ollie Gordon II was seen screaming at a coach and emphatically gesturing before teammates gently steered him away.

Gordon would only say he was frustrated he had to exit the game for a concussion test. But it appeared to be much more.

"I just got to keep my composure more," said Gordon, who spearheaded a productive running game with 88 yards on 18 carries.

"It's just one of those things where, you know, it can't be out there exerting energy like that."

Good time for Miami Dolphins to head into bye week

Frustration. Yes. Perhaps even an issue with a call or just wanting more. And even a sign it's a good time for a break.

But a competitor briefly losing his cool on the sideline of a game in which the Dolphins could not finish when it came to one play, one series and, once again, one game, is not cause for alarm.

To a man, this team remains connected and knows everything about this off week — the Dolphins return for an Oct. 25 game at the Jets — will be related to the process. Everything from rest, rehabilitation and preparation.

"It would be a good time for us to look hard and evaluate the players, evaluate the scheme, evaluate how we're coaching, evaluate what certain guys can do, and take a hard look and then come back and go back to work," coach Jeff Hafley said. "That's just … going to be who we are. We're going to roll up our sleeves and this group's going to work. And I know that they're going to.

"This is not going to be a group that starts going backward and pointing fingers."

Sure, the frustration of another semi-close loss permeated the locker room. It could be said for the first time in three weeks Miami did not take a step forward as it did at home against the Kansas City Chiefs (although the margin was two touchdowns) and a five-point loss at Minnesota.

Although this will be recorded as a one-score game, Miami trailed by 18 points entering the fourth quarter. The Dolphins scored with 45 seconds to play to narrow the margin.

Still, the faint silver lining is it wasn't a blowout, and this team is very much connected and serious about the work ahead.

"We've lost five in a row," linebacker Jordyn Brooks said. "So I think this bye week will be good for us if we treat it the right way. Use that time to self reflect. Everybody look at what you can do better individually. And use that time to rest and recover and kind of reset and try to come back and put on a better result."

Losing is hard on someone who played for Alabama

Many of these players are not used to losing. Certainly not those who came from powerhouse college programs, like rookie guard Kadyn Proctor, who in three years at Alabama never lost five games in a season.

Proctor said being 0-5 is a "big eye opener." But you have to look at the journey without ever considering where it will end.

"All I'm focused on is just doing my part," he said. "That's really all it's about. We have the guys out there to win games. Just like this one was close. We played to the end. We just need to put it together from the start to finish."

Robinson will use a few days to take his mind off football but still continue building trust with his teammates.

"I don't want to be 0-5, but I'm here," he said. "I'm fighting for these guys. I'm going to keep playing hard for these guys and these coaches and we're going to get it right. I believe we're going to turn it around."

As for Hafley, he will re-evaluate all that's happened in the first five games of his professional head coaching career. That will answer some questions about the details.

But for the bigger picture, he already knows what he wants to see when his team arrives in the Meadowlands in two weeks.

"I want to see more consistency," he said. "I want to see better execution. I want to see the same fight. I want to see the same energy. I want to see the same connection. We need to execute better, and that's all of us. That's not me just talking about the players. That's everybody."

Tom D'Angelo is a senior sports columnist and reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at tdangelo@pbpost.com.

articles.title: Jaguars’ Cam Little reps Manchester United after heroic ‘dream’ achievement
articles.summary: Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little, who grew up playing soccer and watching the Premier League every weekend, was the hero in Sunday afternoon’s dramatic...
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little, who grew up playing soccer and watching the Premier League every weekend, was the hero in Sunday afternoon's dramatic Week 5 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles , drilling a game-winning 57-yard field goal before a crowd of 61,322 at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London.

"To do it in that stadium, it feels like I've achieved my goal of playing professional soccer, even though I'm playing pro football," said Little, who wore a retro Manchester United away jersey with "Ronaldo 7" on the back during his postgame news conference.

The 23-year-old also celebrated by sprinting toward the opposite end zone with his teammates chasing him before spreading his arms in a gesture inspired by England and Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham.

Little's opportunity came after running back Ameer Abdullah returned Philadelphia's kickoff 53 yards, leaving Jacksonville with one second to attempt the winning field goal. The Eagles had moved ahead 17-16 through Jake Elliott's 48-yard kick with eight seconds remaining, seemingly putting the game beyond Jacksonville's reach.

However, Abdullah's return gave the Jaguars one final chance with one second remaining, and Little converted from 57 yards as the clock expired. Defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton handled the long-snapping duties after regular long snapper Ross Matiscik suffered a shoulder injury. Hamilton had previously sent a high snap that contributed to Little missing an extra point, but the pair connected on the final attempt.

Jacksonville's comeback victory also featured two touchdown receptions by wide receiver Parker Washington. He opened the scoring with a 51-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter before hauling in quarterback Trevor Lawrence's 27-yard fourth-down pass with 3:20 remaining in the fourth quarter. Washington finished with six receptions for 124 yards.

Lawrence completed 24 of 39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and one interception. His late scoring connection with Washington initially put the Jaguars ahead 16-14, although Little missed the extra point. Elliott's subsequent field goal momentarily restored the Eagles' advantage.

Jacksonville also overcame two unsuccessful goal-line possessions, including a fourth-and-goal stop at Philadelphia's one-yard line just before halftime. Meanwhile, the Eagles managed only 22 rushing yards while playing without leading rusher Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith.

The win extended the Jaguars' winning streak to three games and improved the team to 4-1 , keeping it atop the AFC South early in the season, while Philadelphia fell to 2-3 after losing its third consecutive game.

Jacksonville will remain in London for its next matchup, hosting division rival the Houston Texans at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.

articles.title: 5 Biggest Letdowns From NFL Week 5 on Sunday, Including the Commanders
articles.summary: Another action-packed football Sunday is in the books, and now it’s time to reflect on the biggest letdowns from NFL […]
articles.body:
Another action-packed football Sunday is in the books, and now it's time to reflect on the biggest letdowns from NFL Week 5. This week, that list includes the Washington Commanders, but they're certainly not alone.

Even though the Philadelphia Eagles weren't expected to win on Sunday after seeing their All-Pro right tackle retire and trading their starting center just days earlier, Jake Elliott gave the team a one-point lead with just eight seconds remaining. It looked like the win was in the bag. Somehow the Eagles allowed a 53-yard kick return that set up a game-winning 57-yard field goal from Cam Little. It's a huge disappointment considering the Eagles looked like they were on their way to advancing to 3-2 rather than 2-3.

It's not that Jayden Daniels played poorly, because he actually had a great game. Yet, what everyone will remember is the fact that the Washington Commanders' QB1 has a chance to kill the clock and let Drew Stevens kick a game-winning field goal. Only, the QB failed to find a target near the sidelines or get the ball out of bounds, and ended up taking a game-ending sack instead. Rather than advancing to 2-3, the Commanders end up at 1-3-1 with a tie.

Two weeks ago, the Las Vegas Raiders were undefeated. Now, they're suddenly an average 3-2 team that just got crushed by the New England Patriots, 45-17. With the Bills and Rams up next, suddenly the Raiders need a wake-up call; otherwise, they'll be below .500 in short order. One issue is a lackluster rushing game that averaged a paltry 2.1 yards per carry on 18 attempts, finishing with just 38 yards and a touchdown.

After three consecutive wins, the Cleveland Browns' outlook was starting to look pretty good, especially with the New York Jets up next. Yet, Todd Monken's team failed this test, falling 17-12 to the Jets. The rushing offense remains ineffective, even if Sunday's effort, averaging 4.0 yards per carry, was a tick above their season norm of 3.7 YPC. This time, it was an offensive line that couldn't protect Deshaun Watson at all, causing the former Pro Bowl QB to tie a career-high with eight sacks, finishing with a total of 102 passing yards after the loss of 53 yards via sacks. Cleveland can't afford to be that incapable on offense again.

Los Angeles Chargers fans have gotten used to it this season, but they let their spectators down again on Sunday, falling to 0-5. Justin Herbert had a chance to lead his team on a game-winning drive, only to toss an interception to Denver Broncos safety Brandon Jones instead. It was Herbert's second turnover of the day, and after taking five sacks for a loss of 39 yards, the Chargers' passing offense ended with just 82 yards on the day. Jim Harbaugh may like a throwback offense, but that's a bit too far back.
