articles.summary: SEATTLE (AP) — San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel was ruled out of Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks with a hamstring injury after he le...
articles.body:
SEATTLE (AP) — San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Deebo Samuel was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks with a hamstring injury after he left the field late in the third quarter.

Samuel fumbled at the 49ers 35 and was motionless on the field for several seconds before limping to the sideline.

Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe recovered the ball and the Seahawks kicked a field goal four plays later to extend their lead to 26-21.

Samuel had two receptions for 21 yards and two carries for 4 yards before leaving the game.

The game had seven total turnovers through three quarters.

articles.title: How a nightmare week in the NFC East impacts all four head coaches
articles.summary: The Giants, Commanders, Eagles and Cowboys all had a tough week.
articles.body:
Week 5 of the NFL season was not kind to the NFC East, as all four teams in the division had frustrating endings to their games.

After the Dallas Cowboys underwhelmed on Thursday night, the Philadelphia Eagles faltered across the pond in the morning while the New York Giants and Washington Commanders played to a tie in the early afternoon. Overall, each of the four teams experienced maddening moments in their games, leading their fans to wonder what could have been.

Still, the four teams didn't have an equal intensity of frustrations in Week 5. In some cases, the team's had coach admitted after the game to costing them the game, while in others, the Week 5 was just a speed bump in the 2026 season.

With all four NFC East teams leaving much to be desired, here's a breakdown of how each result impacts the four head coaches in the division.

While the Commanders didn't lose on Sunday, settling for a tie against the Giants may have put Dan Quinn in a difficult hole. Washington was up two possessions for most of the game but blew a 14-point lead as New York forced overtime with a late rally.

Then, in overtime, the Commanders were in prime position to win the game when the offense bungled the final play of the game, allowing the time on the clock to expire. Instead of getting a chance to kick a field goal and win the game, Washington collected a tie.

"Leaving tonight with a tie feels like a loss," Quinn said after the game . "The right call is to clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot, and that's my responsibility and nobody else's,"

Quinn's seat is perhaps the hottest among the NFC East head coaches, and giving away a tie in a game the team should've won didn't help. Washington is now 1-3-1 in the division, currently in last place, which is why a win vs. New York would have been so important.

In the opening game on Sunday in London, the Eagles lost in catastrophic fashion to the Jacksonville Jaguars After taking a one-point lead with just eight seconds left, Philadelphia allowed a big kickoff return to the Jaguars that led to a game-winning Jacksonville field goal.

Sirianni took the blame after the game, saying that the kicking team should have sent the ball out of the endzone.

"I didn't make the right decision, and I lost us that game. And that's what I said to our guys," he said . "I [didn't] make the decision that I should make at the end of that game, and I cost us that one. And I put that fully on me."

The final sequence is the talking point, but Sirianni was already under the spotlight for the Eagles' lack of production on offense, which didn't improve on Sunday. While the Eagles probably won't fire Sirianni midseason, he does need to turn things around to quiet the outside noise.

Overall, Sirianni's tough day on Sunday will only anger Philadelphia fans even more.

The Cowboys were grateful for the NFC East's rough Sunday, as it helped put distance between the team's brutal loss on Thursday night. Brian Schottenheimer's squad lost at home on a short week to the winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers and undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels, falling to 2-3 in the process.

Schottenheimer hoped new defensive coordinator Christian Parker would help fix a broken defense from 2025, but the unit hasn't been much better this year. Instead, the Cowboys once again face the task of needing their offense to overcome their defensive miscues.

Still, Schottenheimer gets the benefit that the Cowboys do not typically make coaching changes, so his job doesn't appear to be in jeopardy. Jerry Jones last fired a head coach midseason in 2010, and every Cowboys head coach since 2000 got at least three seasons at the helm.

While Schottenheimer still needs to make the playoffs to ease any job concerns, his seat likely not as hot as Quinn's or Sirianni's. Dallas also benefits the most from no team winning on Sunday, as the team could feel like it caught a break.

Harbaugh's status as the Giants head coach is in a different galaxy than his three counterparts. Harbaugh has the Giants in first place in his first season as head coach, and New York fans are thrilled that the team is just competing at a high level.

Even the tie vs. Washington on Sunday shows why the Giants are happy with Harbaugh. New York came back from down two touchdowns to force overtime, and the defense held firm late in the game to secure the tie. While the Giants blew a few chances to score in the extra frame, New York fought its way to get to that point.

Harbaugh is not without his faults, as he has made a few decisions in the first few weeks that he probably wants back. Even with the tie, though, Giants fans are more relieved that they didn't lose on the road to a division rival on Sunday.

articles.title: 3 NASCAR Chase Drivers Suffer Brutal Setbacks at Charlotte
articles.summary: Three NASCAR Chase drivers endured miserable afternoons at Charlotte Motor Speedway. Bubba Wallace, William Byron and Ty Gibbs all finished 34th or worse, le...
articles.body:
For three NASCAR Cup Series championship contenders, Sunday's Bank of America 400 at Charlotte Motor Speedway was effectively over long before the checkered flag.

Bubba Wallace, William Byron and Ty Gibbs entered Charlotte hoping to gain ground in the championship Chase. Instead, all three finished 34th or worse, taking a significant hit with just four races remaining in the season.

None entered Sunday among the top three in points, but that hardly made the results less damaging. All three were already chasing championship leader Kyle Larson , and Charlotte offered an opportunity to close the gap.

Instead, the afternoon made their championship paths considerably more difficult.

Bubba Wallace and William Byron Caught in Violent Charlotte Crash

Wallace and Byron saw their races unravel in a frightening multi-car accident in Turn 2 near the end of Stage 1.

The incident began when Alex Bowman lost control of his No. 48 Chevrolet and shot up the track, collecting Wallace and Byron in a heavy collision.

Wallace's No. 23 Toyota sustained extensive damage. Safety personnel brought a stretcher to his car, but he was able to climb out and walk to the ambulance under his own power. He was subsequently evaluated and released from the infield care center.

The accident also ended Byron's afternoon, leaving Hendrick Motorsports with two badly damaged cars.

Wallace was credited with 37th place, while Byron finished 39th, last in the 39-car field. Bowman finished 38th.

Those results were particularly costly given where the two Chase drivers stood entering Charlotte.

Wallace began the race 10th in points, 137 behind Larson. Byron was 12th, facing a 160-point deficit.

Neither could afford to lose more ground, especially with so few races remaining.

Ty Gibbs Also Endures Miserable Charlotte Afternoon

Ty Gibbs wasn't involved in the Wallace-Byron accident, but his afternoon proved nearly as disappointing.

The Joe Gibbs Racing driver finished 34th after completing 200 of the scheduled 267 laps, ending his race eight laps behind the leaders.

Gibbs entered Charlotte eighth in the standings, 110 points behind Larson. Of the three drivers, he began the afternoon with the strongest championship position.

That made his result particularly painful.

While Gibbs avoided the massive wreck that eliminated Wallace and Byron, he still left Charlotte with a finish that did little to help his title pursuit.

With the Chase heading to Phoenix, Talladega, Martinsville and Homestead-Miami, there are still opportunities to recover. But NASCAR's 2026 championship format offers no reset to erase a bad afternoon.

For Wallace, Byron and Gibbs, Charlotte was exactly the kind of race they needed to avoid.

And with only four races left, there is increasingly little room to make up the damage.

articles.title: More than 10,000 runners take part in Staten Island Half
articles.summary: Staten Island takes center stage as more than 10,000 runners, including hometown favorite Vinny Guadagnino, race through the borough in the sold-out NYRR Sta...
articles.body:
More than 10,000 runners took part in the sold-out NYRR Staten Island Half, one of New York Road Runners' marquee fall races and a key stop on the road to the TCS New York City Marathon.

The event also features nearly 200 children ages 2 to 11 participating in Rising NYRR races at SIUH Community Park, home of the Staten Island FerryHawks.

The half marathon draws runners from across the region to a 13.1-mile course that showcases Staten Island's waterfront, with views of New York Harbor and the city skyline. The route passes Fort Wadsworth and several of the borough's parks before finishing on Bay Street.

Among this year's participants is Staten Island native and "Jersey Shore" television personality Vinny Guadagnino, who is running the race in his home borough for the second time. He is joined by Pedro Mendez of Goldfinger Track Club.

The event also highlights members of the 2026 Team Inspire, a group of runners recognized for their personal stories and journeys.

One of those runners is Mildred Baker, 80, of the Bronx. After joining the NYRR Striders program for older adults in her late 70s, Baker completed her first half marathon in 2025 at the United Airlines NYC Half and is preparing to run her first marathon at age 80.

Also participating is Julianna Mangano, 26, of Staten Island. Organizers said she began running after her cousin and best friend suffered a cardiac event during a routine run. She has since been inspired to become a professional sports athletic trainer and EMT, running to "finish the run that he never got to finish."

The Staten Island Half serves as the final New York Road Runners-hosted race before marathon week and is the sixth and final event in the organization's Five-Borough Series. For many runners, it offers a final opportunity to test themselves ahead of the TCS New York City Marathon.

The event also underscores New York Road Runners' year-round presence in Staten Island through community programming, including NYRR Open Runs and NYRR Striders activities. According to the organization, more than 1,100 NYRR members live on Staten Island and more than 4,700 Staten Island students participate in Rising New York Road Runners programs.

articles.title: Houston Texans' defense finds its form in win over Titans as Will Anderson Jr. records 3 sacks
articles.summary: With DeMeco Ryans calling plays, the Texans played like they were expected to at the start of the season in a dominant win over Tennessee.
articles.body:
It might have been against the Tennessee Titans but the Houston Texans ' defense played like the unit many people were expecting to start the year in Sunday's 26-3 win .

The defense forced two turnovers, leading to two scoring drives. Tennessee averaged just 3.2 yards per play and failed to score after a field goal on its first drive. Defensive Player of the Year candidate Will Anderson Jr. sacked Cam Ward three times in a single quarter.

It was the most complete defensive performance of the season, and it came in DeMeco Ryans' first game back calling plays .

"The defense did an outstanding job today," Ryans said.

Beating up on the Titans is nothing new for the fourth-year head coach and the Texans.

Houston is now 6-1 against Tennessee in the Ryans era. In four of those wins, the defense held the Titans' offense to 204 yards or less. Those four games top Houston's leaderboard for fewest yards allowed in a regular-season game since 2018. Sunday's win was the third time Tennessee has been held to under three points by the Texans since 2023.

It started in the middle of the field with the starting linebacker duo of Azeez Al-Shaair and Jake Hansen. Hanson, starting his fourth straight game with Henry To'oTo'o out, has continued to get better as the season progressed. After notching a career-high 12 tackles last week, Hansen snagged his first career interception and notched the first two passes defended of his career.

Al-Shaair returned after missing last week's game with a groin injury and finished with a game-high 11 tackles.

"Azeez is our field general," Ryans said. "He's our communicator. He's the man in the middle."

There were a lot more bright spots to go around. Titans rookie wide receiver Carnell Tate had a breakout performance last week against the Baltimore Ravens with nine catches for 145 yards. But the Houston defensive backs held Tate to just one catch for 6 yards on five targets. Defensive tackle Kayden McDonald, one of Houston's two second-round picks in the most recent draft, made his NFL debut, starting the game and finishing with two tackles.

Then there was Anderson. For the first three quarters, Anderson had been relatively quiet as other players led the way. Then, as the Titans opened up the passing attack in the fourth quarter trying to stage a comeback, Anderson turned silence in a statement.

He sacked Ward three times over the course of nine minutes, two of them coming on fourth down. It was the second three-sack game of his career.

Anderson is also now up to 7½ sacks on the season and on pace to shatter his previous career high of 12.

"The guy is a tenacious player, relentless every single snap," Ryans said. "There's no better competitor, no better person than Will Anderson. So to see him go out and dominate the game by getting three sacks is just an outstanding performance by him."

It wasn't all bright spots, however, as Jalen Pitre left the game with a shoulder injury in the second half. Ryans said after the game the severity of the knock was unknown. Pitre plays a key and versatile role in the defensive system, and any time missed would be a huge loss.

How much can be taken away from a victory over a team that's 6-33 since the start of the 2024 season is also up for debate. The AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars, now 4-1, present a much bigger challenge next Sunday in London than a struggling Titans offense.

But Houston now has something to build upon, and a chance to play without the weight of winlessness on their backs.

"Defensive football always works together," Ryans said. "To me, it's a beautiful puzzle. When it's put together the proper way, with the D line harassing the quarterback, speeding him up, it allows our coverage guys to have a little bit more freedom. Whether we're pressing, whether we're off, that doesn't matter."

articles.title: Lions dominate in all 3 phases in blowout win over Cardinals, 45-21
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions made a statement with their dominant win over the Arizona Cardinals.
articles.body:
For the first quarter of the game, it looked like the Detroit Lions' woes were here to stay. The Arizona Cardinals outgained the Lions 84 yards to -9, and it seemed Detroit was going to head into their bye week thinking about massive changes.

But the rest of the game was a complete reversal. The Lions defense forced five straight three-and-outs. The offense shook off three straight three-and-outs to start the game, and scored on seven straight drives, including six touchdowns. The rout was on as the Lions were finally firing on all cylinders: offense, defense, and special teams. It ended in a decisive 45-21 victory for Detroit.

The win moves the Lions to 3-2, tied with both the Packers and Bears for second place in the NFC North—all behind the undefeated Vikings.

The Lions won the coin toss and opted to take the ball—a shift in their normal strategy. But it didn't help provide a spark as Detroit quickly went three-and-out following two short runs and a sack on third down by Caridnals safety Budda Baker.

The Lions defense took over and ran into some familiar problems. Mainly, their third-and-long woes. On third-and-11, Jacoby Brissett hit Kendrick Bourne for a 22-yard gain, beating Roger McCreary in man-to-man coverage. That moved Arizona into field goal range. Then on third-and-6, the Cardinals converted again on a pass to Michael Wilson for 8. They faced yet another third-and-long, but Detroit got a stop…. to force a fourth-and-1. Arizona opted to go for it, and a trick play—reverse pass—made for an easy conversion.

One play later, the Cardinals cashed in on a 1-yard touchdown catch to Teagan Quitoriano. 7-0 Cardinals.

Detroit answered with another three-and-out. Goff was sacked on first down, and he failed to connect with Isaac TeSlaa on third-and-long.

But Detroit's defense finally responded with a three-and-out of their own. Brissett tried to target McBride downfield, but he was covered well by Jack Campbell, helping force an incomplete pass.

Tom Kennedy tried to provide a spark with a 22-yard punt return into Cardinals territory. It didn't work. The Lions went incomplete pass, sack/fumble, screen pass for 2 yards.

Detroit's defense got another three-and-out, thanks to a pressure from Alim McNeill on second down and sticky coverage from D.J. Reed on third down. Tom Kennedy got another decent punt return (11 yards), but his lower body bent awkwardly when tackles, injuring the special teamer. Kennedy was eventually carted off and listed as questionable to return with a knee injury.

The Lions, again, failed to convert a third down, still looking for their first conversion of the game. But on fourth-and-3, at midfield the Lions went for it, and Sam LaPorta made an impressive contested catch—and got another 15 yard tacked on due to a roughness penalty.

Jahmyr Gibbs followed it up with a 16-yard run to move the Lions inside the 5-yard line. Two plays later, Gibbs was in for the touchdown. 7-7 tie.

Detroit answered with another strong defensive series. McCreary batted down a third-down pass to get off the field, and Amon-Ra St. Brown, filling in for Kennedy, took the punt return 30 yards into Cardinals territory. Luckily for Detroit, they recovered a late fumble by St. Brown on the play.

On the subsequent drive, LaPorta came up with a big play on third-and-12, juking a defender and diving forward to pick up what appeared to be a first down. Officials ruled him short and that ruling stood upon a Lions challenge. That set up a fourth-and-1 from the Cardinals' 37-yard line. Detroit ran a play action and Goff found a wide-open LaPorta for a 37-yard touchdown and a 14-7 Lions lead.

The Cardinals went three-and-out for their fourth straight possession after another pass breakup from McCreary, and a deep shot on third down that fell incomplete when the receiver fell down.

Detroit immediately threatened again thanks to a screen pass to Gibbs for 23 yards. Then Gibbs had an excellent rep in pass protection, allowing Goff to find Brock Wright for 11 yards. Then the Lions running back picked up 18 yards on the ground to get into the red zone. But on third-and-4 from inside the 10-yard line, Goff missed an open Isaac TeSlaa for the touchdown. Detroit made the controversial decision to go for it, but Goff and Jameson Williams proved Dan Campbell right with an 8-yard touchdown. 21-7 Lions.

Detroit forced a fifth straight three-and-out thanks to a coverage (!!) sack on a third-and-short. Brissett couldn't find anyone open, and DJ Wonnum brought him down for the first sack of the game.

The Lions offense avoided a return three-and-out with a well-time screen pass to St. Brown for 11 yards, pushing the game into the two-minute warning. Out of the break, the Lions pulled off a reverse flea flicker screen for 18 yards.

But Detroit's drive stalled in field goal range when they failed to convert a third-and-6 with a conservative draw play. Jake Bates lined up for a 46-yard field goal and nailed to to move the game to 24-7 Lions with 53 second remaining.

With no timeouts, the Cardinals looked to cut into the lead and possibly double-up at each side of halftime. They converted a third-and-10 with a 22-yard strike up the seam to Bourne. But Wonnum's second sack of the game essentially ended their bid. Rookie Keith Abney picked off a hail mary attempt to close out an impressive second quarter from the entire Lions team.

Arizona started the second half with an explosive play. A missed assignment in the secondary left a wide open Elijah Higgens for a 38-yard gain.

But the defense stiffened up from there. D.J. Reed made a nice tackle for loss in the run game, and Alim McNeill followed it up with a sack.

That set up a third-and-21, and the Cardinals just checked down to improve field goal range. But Chad Ryland pushed the 53-yard field goal wide right.

The Lions were putting together a promising drive until St. Brown absorbed a big hit and fumbled the ball—turning a 6-yard gain into a 6-yard loss when Tate Ratledge fell on the ball. But the Lions dug out of the hole with a 39-yard bomb to Jameson Williams for his second touchdown of the day. 31-7 Lions.

The Cardinals needed to score and they needed to score quick to get back in the game. They methodically worked their way down to the field with a steady and productive passing game, including a third-and-2 conversion to Trey McBride that set the Cardinals up in the red zone. Then Brissett found a wide open Quitoriano for a 13-yard touchdown. 31-14 Lions.

Detroit quickly answered, though. Goff found a wide-open St. Brown for a 36-yard gain, and Gibbs followed it up with a 22-yard gain on a toss play all the way down to Arizona's 2-yard line. The Lions struggled to punch it in, but Jared Goff eventually plunged in for Detroit's third touchdown on fourth down. 38-14 Lions.

On the last play of the third quarter, the Cardinals kept a drive alive with a third-and-9 conversion to McBride for 11.

The Cardinals got a free extra 15 yards after Levi Onwuzurike roughed the passer, which moved Arizona comfortably into Lions territory. It appeared they were about to score again, but Detroit's disciplined defense on third and fourth-and-short forced a turnover on downs. It was Aidan Hutchinson who wrapped up Brissett for the sack after fantastic coverage.

Nursing a 24-point lead with 13 minutes left, Detroit turned to Gibbs and the run game to try to bleed the rest of the clock. Gibbs had gains of 8, 11, and 15 yards on consecutive runs to move midfield. A 19-yard pass to Laporta kept the drive moving, and a 7-yard wide receiver screen to St. Brown converted a third-and-long. Eventually, Gibbs plunged in for Detroit's sixth touchdown of the game. 45-14 Lions.

The Cardinals would add on a late touchdown, with this incredible catch from Trey McBride. 45-21 Lions.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy Reveals Why Patrick Graham Was Moved to Sideline
articles.summary: PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham moved from the box to the sideline for Sunday’s game against the […]
articles.body:
PITTSBURGH — Pittsburgh Steelers defensive coordinator Patrick Graham moved from the box to the sideline for Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts.

Graham has called the first four games as Steelers defensive coordinator from the box, something that he said before the season that he prefers.

After T.J. Watt's viral outburst against the Cleveland Browns, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy decided to move Graham to the sideline for better communication.

"Back in training camp, when you get to the point where you're getting ready to play preseason games, I had really two rosters, as far as who's up and who's down," McCarthy said after Sunday's win. "After the Green Bay game, this was frankly my preference, to have Patrick and Joe [Whitt] on the field. We gave it a shot the other way.

"We'll evaluate this. I just felt it needed to be different. I think communication on game day is such a critical part [of] your process … We can't have things that we miss that we're talking about after the fact. There's nothing better than face-to-face communication. I think when your coordinators and your play-callers are on the field, it's definitely the best case … The communication component is the priority."

The Steelers' other play-caller, head coach Mike McCarthy, is obviously on the sideline. The Steelers have had assistant head coach Joe Whitt Jr. running the defense on the sideline. It's unclear who will replace Graham in the booth.

The team's Week 4 loss to the Browns included heated communication between players and both players, with Aaron Rodgers and McCarthy getting into it and Watt yelling through a headset at Graham.

McCarthy confirmed that the players didn't have an input on the decision.

"Didn't ask [the players]. We've been talking about it since the preseason," he said.

Linebacker Payton Wilson and safety Jaquan Brisker noticed a big difference with Graham on the sideline.

"He just brought a sense of poise and comfort," Wilson said. "When giving up an explosive here or there, he was there to show what went on, show us how we are going to fix it, show us how he is going to help us. It was really cool having him down here. Coach Joe Whitt, just the experience and poise they bring."

"[Graham] on the sideline, (there was) more communicating," Brisker said. "Giving us a lot of dialogue. Telling us what he wants. What he's going to call. It was great. The dialogue was great. The communication between all the coaches and things like that. It was amazing."

Alan Saunders and Brendan Howe provided reporting from Pittsburgh.

articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have been banged up along their defensive line all year with Alfred Collins, C.J. West, Andrew Farmer II and Mikail Kamara on injured reserve. Mykel Williams was just activated this week, and Nick Bosa has been out as well.

On Sunday, the 49ers lost another key piece to their defensive front as defensive end/linebacker Khalid Kareem suffered an injury on a first-and-10 completion between Sam Darnold and Jaxson Smith-Njigba in the fourth quarter.

Kareem signed with the 49ers just before their Week 1 matchup with the Los Angeles Rams in Australia, and he's been in the mix on the edge since then. San Francisco will roll with Williams, Keion White, Romello Height (with a club on one hand) and Ogbo Okoronkwo if Kareem can't go.

Cincinnati Bengals running back Chase Brown rushed 13 times for just 39 yards in Week 5 against the Miami Dolphins , and he had three receptions for 21 yards on four targets.

articles.title: Chiefs vs. Chargers odds: Chiefs opens as 7.5-point favorite against divisional foe
articles.summary: The early season has zapped the buzz between the Kansas City and Los Angeles AFC West rivalry.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will host a reeling Los Angeles Chargers team in Week 6 at Arrowhead stadium. The AFC West showdown lacks the buzz it has brought in recent years.

Before the season, few would have expected the opposite directions these teams find themselves going. The Chiefs are the AFC's lone unbeaten squad at 4-0, now coming off of their Week 5 bye week. The Chargers are the league's biggest surprises after dropping to 0-5 following a sloppy 23-17 loss on Sunday to the Denver Broncos .

According to FanDuel Sportsbook , Kansas City opened as a 7.5-point favorite in the game.

The Chiefs have been favored in each game this season, and they have rounded back into form after missing the playoffs in 2025. For the Chargers, virtually everything that could go wrong has. The team played against Denver down two starting wideouts and a top defensive talent in safety Derwin James. Quarterback Justin Herbert also played behind multiple backups along the offensive line.

Not surprisingly, Herbert will be entering Week 6 coming off of one of the worst performances of his career. He will try to get on track against a rested Kansas City squad.

Before the bye, the Chiefs' last action saw them defeat the Las Vegas Raiders on the road, bringing them to 2-0 in AFC West contests. Los Angeles won both 2025 contests with Kansas City, including the season opener in Brazil and a Week 15 contest at Arrowhead Stadium that saw star quarterback Patrick Mahomes lost for the season with a torn ACL.

articles.title: NLCS Game 1 – Dodgers at Brewers discussion
articles.summary: Who will represent the Senior Circuit in the 2026 World Series?
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers kick off the championship series this Sunday, with a chance to represent the National League in the World Series. These two franchises have met three times in the NLCS, with Los Angeles taking both previous series in 2018 and 2025.

The Brewers come into the series following a franchise-record 103-win season and looking to avenge last year's sweep at the hands of the Dodgers en route to their World Series win. The Dodgers look to duplicate their dominant pitcher performance from last year, when Milwaukee only averaged one run per game against them in the sweep. Now sporting trade deadline acquisition Tarik Skubal, Los Angeles is trying to keep the starting rotation edge. But, Milwaukee will have Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson going in the first two games, giving them a better chance against the Dodgers compared to last postseason.

These two franchises are the only MLB teams with at least 86 wins in the last nine full seasons, with Milwaukee having the best record in baseball the past two seasons. Los Angeles is chasing a chance to win their third consecutive World Series and become the first NL team to achieve that feat, and the first since the New York Yankees did so in 1998-2000.

The game starts at 7 PM Kauffman Standard Time, live on FOX, FOX Deportes, and FOX One. ESPN Radio will also provide national coverage of this game.

Who are you rooting for on the NL side of the bracket? Can the Brewers dethrone the Dodgers, or is another World Series berth for Los Angeles inevitable?

articles.title: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany talks the Joshua Kimmich and Tom Bischof factor
articles.summary: FC Bayern’s coach is aware of the media’s tricks, especially when it comes to singling out his players
articles.body:
It's no secret that Tom Bischof is a highly coveted talent who deserves more playing time for Bayern Munich and the German national football team, the latter of which he performed brilliantly with during the international break. However, it also comes at a time when Joshua Kimmich is on the receiving end of unfounded claims that he holds the team back, when he was in fact clearly misused in his role—exacerbated to some extent by Jürgen Klopp's massive squad.

Bischof's coach at Bayern, Vincent Kompany, knows that the correlation in performance (and perhaps playing time) between club and country should not be blown out of proportion. Instead, he's taking the positive performances from his players as they are and will not draw conclusions from seemingly nothing.

"We've only played six matches so far. The national team doesn't play a part in my decision on the starting XI. I'm absolutely delighted when the players come back feeling positive. But if that's not the case, they can put it it behind them there and then," Kompany said (as captured by X account @iMiaSanMia ). "We recently beat Union 7–0. I learned that with Belgium – things didn't always go perfectly with the national team. Although I was at my best during my club career, I often came back feeling down. That's when I learned to leave those feelings behind with the national team. That's how I handle it now as a coach, too. The players should bring the good things back to the club and leave the bad ones with the national team."

Kompany immediately clocked that the question was indirectly about Kimmich, which, if answered incorrectly, could cause a rift between players or start a media frenzy. The 40-year-old Belgian once again reiterated his disinterest in the discourse and made his stance clear: "As for these questions about Bischof and Kimmich – I know that's what you were thinking about although you didn't mention the name – I haven't forgotten how our last few club games went, and haven't forgotten who played well against Union Berlin, Bodø, Dortmund in the Super Cup, Stuttgart. I take that into account."

articles.title: Giants-Commanders ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’: Plenty of credit, and blame, to go around
articles.summary: Let’s review the game in our unique ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style.
articles.body:
If I were writing this from a Washington Commanders' angle, the brutal clock management by Washington at the end of Sunday's overtime tie would receive a massive "Wet Willie." I'm writing from a New York Giants angle, though, so maybe it should get "Kudos."

You decide. I'm flummoxed. As, I think is everyone else with how Sunday's 27-27 game ended up.

Before we get to the 'Kudos & Wet Willies,' a couple of absolutely wild numbers.

Per the FOX broadcast, the Giants had lost 24 straight games when trailing at halftime. Well, at least now they have not lost 25 straight.

From ESPN Insights , comes this unbelievable nugget. Entering today, the Giants were 0-230 since 1970 when trailing by 14+ points in the final 8 minutes of regulation. They're now 0-230-1.

Now, here is your 'Kudos & Wet Willies' review.

Jameis Winston — After an uninspiring Week 2 game in his first start, even Winston was wondering if he could still throw the ball. Well, umm, he can.

After a 7 of 16 first half that included a costly sack/fumble, Winston finished 33 of 54 for 326 yards, and three touchdowns. The Giants scored all four times they touched the ball in the second half (three touchdowns, a field goal) and would have scored both times they had the ball in overtime had Dominic Zvada not missed a field goal and Cam Skattebo not fumbled with the game seemingly in hand.

After halftime, Winston was 26 of 38 for 54 yards. He made big throw after big throw, though it is fair to mention that the Giants did get bailed out by a ticky-tack defensive pass interference call that negated a third-quarter interception at the goal line by Washington's Amik Robertson.

Still, credit to Winston. Without a running game to speak of until a 19-yard run by Skattebo in overtime, the veteran quarterback carried the Giants' offense with his arm and some veteran savvy.

The Giants have emphasized ball security with the always-willing-to-take-a-risk Winston. Sunday, per NextGen Stats, this happened:

Winston's 54 pass attempts were the most in a game in his career in which he did not throw an interception. Winston had thrown at least one interception in each of his prior eight career games with 50-or-more pass attempts.

Isaiah Likely — During the first couple of games after Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury, the connection between Likely and Winston looked uncertain. Not Sunday. The talented tight end caught 11 passes on 13 targets for 94 yards and 2 touchdowns. The second touchdown, which pulled the Giants within 27-20 with 7:20 to play, came on a 17-yard pass where Likely barely got across the goal line before fumbling the ball.

NextGen Stats had some details on how Likely did what he did on Sunday:

Isaiah Likely ran 87.0% of his routes from the slot in Week 5, catching 9 of his 11 targets for 78 yards and 2 touchdowns when doing so. Likely now leads all tight ends with 195 receiving yards from the slot entering the afternoon slate. Likely also added an 11-yard reception from a tight alignment and a 5-yard reception from the backfield.

Dru Phillips — Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson was dialing up the pressure, especially as things got dire late in the game. Phillips ended up with two sacks and a big impact on the passing game.

Andru Phillips rushed the passer seven times in Week 5, generating four pressures and two sacks. All four of Phillips' pressures came in under 2.5 seconds. Entering today, Phillips had rushed the passer just 9 times this season, generating two pressures and no sacks.

Malik Nabers — The star wide receiver wanted the ball thrown his way more often, and on Sunday Winston and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy made sure that happened against the Commanders. Nabers was targeted an astounding 20 times. It wasn't always perfect as Nabers missed a couple of opportunities, including a second-half deep ball that might have been a touchdown.

Still, Nabers caught 11 passes for 121 yards. He made a nice grab across the middle for a game-tying 17-yard touchdown with 1:43 to play. He also had receptions of 16, 17, and 20 yards.

This is back-to-back 100-yard receiving games for Nabers.

Abdul Carter — Carter got a sack when he chased down Jayden Daniels from behind. He forced a fumble. Pro Football Focus credited Carter with four hurries. The second-year edge defender was impactful, as has become customary.

Dennard Wilson — So much for the thinking that because of Jayden Daniels' ability to make huge plays with his legs, which he showed with 38- and 26-yard touchdown scrambles, that blitzing was a bad idea. With the Giants trailing in the second half and needing to force things to happen, Wilson threw caution to the wind with Cover Zero blitzes again and again. How often? This often:

Personally, I loved it. And, it helped the Giants stymie the Commanders' offense late in the game. Wilson simply seemed to decide that if the Giants were going to go down, they would go down throwing the biggest haymakers they could. And it worked. Somewhere, Wink Martindale is smiling. And maybe cursing, or lifting a glass, in approval.

Cam Little and the Jacksonville Jaguars — I just can't help jabbing the Philadelphia Eagles a little bit after a 19-17 loss on a 57-yard Little field goal. A game the Eagles took a lead in with :08 to play, only to give up a long kickoff return that put Little in position to be a hero.

Cam Skattebo — Ball security. Ball security. Ball security. John Harbaugh has emphasized it again and again. Sunday, Skattebo's inability to protect the football at a key time cost the Giants a victory in a football game they had in their grasp.

Skattebo fumbled with the Giants at the Commanders 24-yard line with a first down and the game in their hands. Until the ball fell out of Skattebo's.

That is four fumbles for Skattebo this season, the most of any running back in the league. That negated two big runs by Skattebo on that last Giants' overtime drive, a 19-yarder on third-and-2, and a 9-yarder to put the ball in clear field goal range at the Washington 29-yard line.

Washington's clock mismanagement meant Skattebo's fumble did not cause the the Giants to lose, but it certainly prevented them from winning.

Tyler Nubin — Multiple coaching staffs (three defensive backs coaching groups) have tried to address Nubin's propensity to take horrible angles against ballcarriers in the open field. None have succeeded.

For the second time this season, Nubin took an awful angle on a run play that went for a touchdown, but should not have. This time it was a 33-yard run by Jacory Croskey-Merritt on Washington's first drive. Nubin found himself on the bench in favor of Ar'Darius Washington before the end of the first half. Nubin did return to action in the second half, but his job is clearly in jeopardy. As it should be.

The rushing "attack" — Head coach John Harbaugh said during the week that the Giants were " just not good enough yet " running the ball. They certainly did not get any better on Sunday. The Giants ran the ball 28 times for 103 yards, 3.7 yards per carry. That was helped massively to overtime runs of 19 and 9 yards by Skattebo. There was also a 15-yard Winston scramble in there.

For the entirety of regulation, there was really no place for Skattebo, Najee Harris, Tyrone Tracy, or J.J. McCarthy to go. Some will point the finger at offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, and I understand it. The Giants, though, tried a variety of runs with a variety of ballcarriers. They could not block anything. I would guess the run-blocking grades are not going to be good ones when Pro Football Focus releases them.

Winston, Likely, Nabers, and the Commanders' stupidity bailed the Giants out on Sunday. If they are going to continue to have success, though, Harbaugh, Nagy, and run game designer Greg Roman are going to have to get this figured out. Asking Winston to play the way he did on Sunday on a weekly basis is not sustainable.

The McCarthy package — The J.J. McCarthy package was a flop. McCarthy made his Giants debut on Sunday. He was on the field for five plays. McCarthy ran twice for 2 yards. A shovel pass to Darnell Mooney went for a 5-yard loss, but was bailed out by a Washington facemask penalty. A screen pass to Malik Nabers for 14 yards was wiped out by an illegal shift. A zone read handoff to Tyrone Tracy went for a yard.

I appreciate effort of trying some way to involve the quarterback run in the offense, but everything done with McCarthy was predictable. As feared. The run game stunk Sunday, and the McCarthy package didn't help.

Dominic Zvada — The rookie made kicks of 51 and 56 yards, but missed wide right from 50 yards and wide left — badly — from 57 and 46 yards. The 46-yarder in overtime could have given the Giants a victory. The only thing saving this from being a 'Wet Willie' is that the Giants did not lose.

Those were Zvada's first misses after entering the game 9 of 9. Two of the misses were from long distance in difficult conditions, but the first off day of his career was costly.

articles.title: Dodgers’ Dave Roberts showers Brewers with ultimate praise before NLCS Game 1
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers are on a collision course in the National League Championship Series for the second year in a row. The Dodg...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and the Milwaukee Brewers are on a collision course in the National League Championship Series for the second year in a row.

The Dodgers are the two-time defending World Series champions, but the Brewers are widely considered the best team during the 2026 MLB regular season, having won a franchise-record 103 wins — also the best overall in the big leagues by three games. (The Los Angeles Dodgers won 100 games.)

Now that the Dodgers are crossing paths again with Milwaukee , Los Angeles manager Dave Roberts shared his video of the Brewers, who, to his eyes, are a great example of what a baseball team should be .

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"They play baseball the way it's intended," Roberts said, via Bob Nightengale of USA Today.

The Dodgers swept Milwaukee in the same round in 2025, as Milwaukee struggled to find its offense. In that series, the Brewers scored just a run in each game, as Los Angeles swept them in four games. The Dodgers then went on to defeat the Toronto Blue Jays in the World Series, doing it in seven games.

The Brewers don't have the financial might Los Angeles have, but as Roberts implied, play elite baseball. Milwaukee had one of the highest wRC+ in the regular season (107) and the same can be said about their ERA (3.51) . Both numbers are top five in the big leagues overall.

To get to the NLCS, the Dodgers defeated the Atlanta Braves in the NL Division Series Round (3-1), while the Brewers took care of business against the San Diego Padres in the same round (3-1).

articles.title: Drew Petzing’s Lions offense gets its revenge on the Arizona Cardinals
articles.summary: Arizona Cardinals get routed by Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
It's hard to even write about this every week.

The Arizona Cardinals through five weeks are playing some of the worst football in the team's history.

I was in the South endzone at Sun Devil Stadium from 1994. I've seen some awful games.

This is getting to the point of being unwatchable.

Meanwhile, Jonathan Gannon's Packers shut down the Bears.

Drew Petzing's offense just had over 400 yards of offense and 45-points.

Somehow, moving on, which was probably the right move in all three cases, has made this team much, much worse.

Now, the question is; do they keep running it back.

I get it's only week five, but the fact that this team has given 31 or more points in each game since week one, is bad.

Jacoby Brissett has moved to 2-15 as a starter, his 0.118 win percentage is the worst in Arizona Cardinals history (minimum 8 starts).

This is some of the most uninspired football we have seen.

Brissett had 292 yards and three touchdowns, but that second touchdown happened with 4:22 left in the third and the Cardinals down by 24.

The final touchdown came with 2:11 left in the game on maybe the best play of the season by Trey McBride, down 45-14.

Now the 1-4 Arizona Cardinals have to go play the Los Angeles Rams.

So, is it time to see Gardner Minshew? Is it Carson Beck time?

There are way more questions than answers at this point into the Mike LaFleur era.

articles.title: Jared Goff, Jahmyr Gibbs lead the Lions' offensive romp in a 45-21 win over the Cardinals
articles.summary: (AP) — Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, Jahmyr Gibbs added 151 yards rushing and two more scores and the Detroit Lions shook off a slow start by scor...
articles.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. (AP) — Jared Goff threw three touchdown passes, Jahmyr Gibbs added 151 yards rushing and two more scores and the Detroit Lions shook off a slow start by scoring 31 straight points to roll past the Arizona Cardinals 45-21 on Sunday.

Gibbs barreled into the end zone on a 1-yard run in the second quarter and added a 3-yard TD run in the fourth, bouncing off the offensive line before reversing field and finding room to run. The three-time Pro Bowl selection has scored an NFL-record 58 touchdowns before his 25th birthday, passing Lions great Barry Sanders, who had 57.

Jameson Williams had his first multi-TD receiving game, catching touchdowns for 8 and 39 yards for Detroit (3-2).

Arizona (1-4) has lost nine straight home games, a streak that's lasted more than a year.

It was a disappointing, weird afternoon for the Cardinals, who finalized a trade to send receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans in the middle of the first quarter. Harrison was one of the team's five inactives against the Lions and wasn't seen at the stadium.

The No. 4 overall pick in 2024 out of Ohio State has been a major disappointment in the desert and he had just five catches for 85 yards and a touchdown through four games this season.

But the non-Harrison version of the Cardinals wasn't any better Sunday.

Arizona took an early 7-0 lead after a 2-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett to tight end Teagan Quitoriano, but right about the time news of the Harrison deal started spreading, the momentum shifted.

Detroit scored three straight touchdowns and a field goal to take a 24-7 lead into halftime. Tight end Sam LaPorta caught the second of the three TDs, finding himself wide open for a 38-yard catch and run.

Williams added a 39-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter on a perfectly-thrown ball by Goff, who completed 19 of 30 passes for 279 yards. Goff also ran for a 1-yard touchdown.

While the Lions were piling up points, the Cardinals had five straight three-and-out drives during the first half, gaining just 12 total yards. On the sixth drive, Brissett threw an interception that ended the second quarter.

It was a better performance by the Lions' defense, which came into Sunday giving up 31.8 points per game to rank No. 31 in the NFL.

Brissett completed 29 of 47 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. He is 2-15 as the team's starter since taking over for Kyler Murray last season.

Quitoriano finished with two receiving touchdowns, adding a 13-yard catch in the third quarter. Trey McBride also had a 9-yard TD catch late in the fourth quarter.

Lions: LB Devin White (forearm) and KR/PR Tom Kennedy (knee) both left the game and didn't return.

Cardinals: S Wydett Williams Jr. (concussion) was hurt late in the first half.

Cardinals: At the Los Angeles Rams next Sunday.

articles.title: Here's how both the Giants and the Commanders turned a likely victory into a tie
articles.summary: (AP) — With the game tied at 27, the Washington Commanders and New York Giants each had chances to run the clock down and kick a routine field goal to win in...
articles.body:
LANDOVER Md. (AP) — With the game tied at 27, the Washington Commanders and New York Giants each had chances to run the clock down and kick a routine field goal to win in overtime. Here's a recap — call it an oral history of misery — of how each team blew it on Sunday.

2 minutes remaining, the Giants are seemingly in control

It was first-and-10 from the Washington 24. Since it was the third possession of overtime, this was a sudden-death situation. The Giants could have kicked a field goal right then, but Dominic Zvada had already missed from 50, 57 and 46 yards — and New York coach John Harbaugh's tenure in Baltimore ended last season on a missed field goal from 44 yards.

"That field goal is very makeable, but it's not a gimme," Harbaugh said. "I've had some experience with that."

So the plan was to try to advance a little bit closer while also running more time off the clock. The Commanders were out of timeouts — remember that for later — and the Giants could have run so much time off that even if Zvada missed again, Washington would have had no chance to drive the other way and the game would end in a tie.

"That's the strategy we'll probably do next time, too," Harbaugh said.

Skattebo fumbles, giving Washington a lifeline

The Giants could have run the clock down by simply taking a knee a couple of times. Instead, Cam Skattebo took a handoff and was met behind the line of scrimmage. Washington's Daron Payne knocked the ball loose and Shy Tuttle recovered for the Commanders.

"There's 11 guys on the other team just screaming at you," Skattebo said. "Telling you you messed up, it's your fault, you sold the game, everything. You get that."

55 seconds left, Washington in field goal range

Two passes and a run had the Commanders across midfield. Then Jayden Daniels threw a pass to Treylon Burks, who went out of bounds with 55 seconds left. It was now first-and-10 from the New York 26. Washington was in the same position the Giants had just squandered — with a chance to run the clock down and try a field goal for the win on the final play.

"Defense did a great job of getting a stop and forcing the turnover," Daniels said. "At that point, it was like, OK, we got to go win this football game."

Rachaad White ran the ball 2 yards to the New York 24 — and the clock started ticking.

27 seconds left, the Commanders are in no rush

Once the clock was under 40 seconds, Washington could have taken a knee, let the time run all the way down and then had Daniels spike the ball with under 5 seconds remaining. Instead, the Commanders went into a huddle, and with 27 seconds to go they were still in it.

The plan was apparently to throw the ball — to someone who could easily get out of bounds. If need be, Daniels could always toss the ball away for a clock-stopping incompletion.

"It's an outside throw or a clock — an out-of-bounds throw, or a clock," coach Dan Quinn said.

13 seconds left, Washington finally snaps the ball

The Commanders broke the huddle and Daniels lined up under center. Someone even went in motion. By the time the play began, the Commanders could not risk having someone tackled in bounds, because the clock could run out.

"We have to stop the clock. We have to know the situation," Daniels said. "We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me."

After the snap, Daniels rolled to his left and Ben Sinnott ran a route toward the sideline. Instead of throwing, Daniels turned inside and was tackled. It's still not clear if he knew Washington was out of timeouts.

"We just got to communicate that," he said. "That's the whole thing. As I said, it starts with me communicating to the whole offense in the huddle, and I think everyone will say that top down."

Washington's fate might have been sealed the moment Daniels was tackled, but the clock would still have stopped if the Commanders could have lined up legally and had the quarterback spike the ball before it expired. It's hard to say how many players realized exactly what the situation was.

Daniels stayed down for a couple seconds, looking around. Tackle Josh Conerly Jr. started making a bit of a spiking motion with his hand as if to tell Daniels what was needed. Sinnett headed back toward the line of scrimmage with nowhere near enough urgency. New York edge rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux stood with his hands on his hips.

Tight end John Bates lined up out wide to the far side, motioning to hurry up.

"The right call is honestly like we can go clock it early and don't put ourselves in that spot," Quinn said. "That is my responsibility."

The clock ran out. Defensive lineman Shelby Harris started waving both arms to indicate the game should be over. Cornerback Deonte Banks leaped in the air, ran across the line of scrimmage, then leaped again in celebration. Quinn ripped off his headset and threw it to the ground.

A tie snatched first from the jaws of victory and then from the jaws of defeat.

"I wanted to get off the field before they could take it away from us, I guess," Harbaugh said. "I was surprised. I can't say that I wasn't. It was a pretty shocking end there."

"I probably won't get reamed as much," he said. "But I'm still going to get reamed."
